title: A grid save can delete text after the file changes tab width.
input: Open a table with rows `col\tval` and `longer\tcontent`, then let the file set `tab=1`. The file now reads `longer content` as one cell, but the editor still shows two inputs. Editing the first input and saving drops `content`. Turning table mode off on disk also lets the stale grid rewrite the body as plain text.
fix: Snapshot the grid at open. Before saving a grid edit, compare its opening cell layout and table mode with the current file, and refuse if either changed.
prevent_detail: Edit one cell after a file option changes the grid and assert that save cannot delete or rewrite untouched cells.

title: A table-only toggle is refused when the file changes the body.
input: Open plain code with rows `A  B` and `C  D`. Change the body on disk, then click Table and Done without editing any cells. The editor sends a body even though the toggle made no text change, so the save is refused. Editing and then restoring the original text also blocks an unrelated caption edit.
fix: Track user changes to body content separately from mode changes. Omit the body when the user made no net content edit.
prevent_detail: Run the conflict matrix through the real editor controls and include a mode-only toggle and a body edit reverted before save.

title: Renaming the node on disk silently drops its open draft.
input: Rename `q` in the file while its editor is open, then click Done with a changed caption. The editor closes without saving or showing a toast. The parent commit showed a conflict toast.
fix: If a changed draft no longer has an editable target, refuse it with a toast that names what happened.
prevent_detail: Rename or delete an open draft target and assert that save leaves the file intact and explains why it was refused.

title: Saving a body edit trims an untouched caption.
input: Open a node with the caption `" Query "` and edit only its body. Done strips the caption's spaces. If the file changed that caption to `"Report"` while the editor was open, the body save is incorrectly refused.
fix: Compare the untrimmed caption with its opening value and trim only a caption the user actually changed.
prevent_detail: Use a caption with outer whitespace in a body-only save test and assert that the caption stays exactly as authored.

title: Awaited compound operands still appear as field producers.
input: With `o.k` initially `10`, `o["k"] += await step()` stores `12` when `step()` resolves to `2`. The graph lists `step()` as a producer and has no `operand` stop. A `.ts` probe with `o.k += <number>step` also lists the operand.
fix: Classify the operand from the assignment that created the pack edge. Keep `&&=`, `||=`, and `??=` on the value path because they can store their right-hand side unchanged.
prevent_detail: Run annotated traces for wrapped compound right-hand sides and require an operand stop whenever the collector strips a wrapper.

title: JSX spreads into lowercase-qualified components miss writes.
input: Spread `const state = { k: 10 }` into `<ui.Editor {...state} />`, where `Editor` sets `props.k = 42`. Solid passes the object to the component, and the later `state.k` read returns `42`. The graph reports `10` as the only producer with no caveat.
fix: Recognize JSX member expressions as component tags regardless of the first letter. Share that check between spread and named props.
prevent_detail: Run the same mutating props fixture with both a bare component name and a lowercase-qualified component name.

title: Objects assigned after declaration lose the mutable caveat.
input: `let o: { k: number }; o = { k: 10 }; const a = o; a.k = 42; return o.k` returns `42`. Both the commit and its parent report `10` as the only producer with no caveat. Replacing an earlier initializer has the same result.
fix: Resolve the binding that receives an object literal on the right of a plain assignment, then run the same mutation check used for declaration initializers.
prevent_detail: Run the same alias-write trace with a declaration initializer, a later assignment, and a reassignment.

title: A wrapped default export can hide a write from another module.
input: One module declares `const state = { k: 10 }` and uses `export default (state)`. An importer runs `Object.assign(state, { k: 42 })`. The exporting module reads `42` at runtime, but both revisions report `10` with no caveat.
fix: Check for an export assignment after removing parentheses and type-only wrappers from the exported expression.
prevent_detail: Use a two-module mutation fixture to verify that wrapping an exported expression does not remove its caveat.

title: Reading an awaited promise result can mark its containing object mutable.
input: `const state = { count: 10, completion: Promise.resolve({ ready: true }) }; const { ready } = await state.completion; return state.count` only reads the promise result and the count. The parent reports `10` with no caveat, but the commit adds `mutable`.
fix: Handle `await` separately from syntax-only wrappers. Preserve the alias for a non-thenable object, but do not treat a read of a known promise's separate result as an escape of its container.
prevent_detail: Pair await-mutation fixtures with read-only controls for scalar destructuring and promise-valued members.

title: Spreading into a known read-only component adds a mutable caveat.
input: Spread `{ k: 10 }` into a local `<View {...state} />` whose only use of props is `return props.k`. Solid leaves `state.k` unchanged. The commit adds `mutable` and the card drops its only-producer answer.
fix: Keep the caveat for unresolved components. When a local component's only prop uses are scalar reads, do not treat the spread as a write.
prevent_detail: Pair a mutating JSX spread fixture with a local component that only reads the same props.

title: Await drops the mutable caveat when its result still aliases the object.
input: Declare `const state: {item: Item | Promise<Item>} = {item: {k: 10}}`, then run `const item = await state.item; item.k = 42`. Reading the non-Promise `state.item.k` returns `42`, but the card names only `10` with no caveat. The parent commit adds `mutable`. The same regression occurs when a getter returns `Promise.resolve(this.item)`.
fix: Keep tracking the awaited result when any operand can pass through unchanged or resolve to shared state. Suppress the caveat for a separate result that is only read.
prevent_detail: Pair a read of a fresh promise result with writes through awaited union values and promises that resolve to shared objects.

title: An object assigned after declaration loses its mutable caveat.
input: `let o: {k: number}; o = {k: 10}; const alias = o; alias.k = 42; return o.k` returns `42`. Both the base and this commit name only `10` with no caveat. Replacing an earlier initializer fails the same way.
fix: Resolve the binding that receives the literal on the right of a plain assignment and run the same mutation check as for a declaration initializer.
prevent_detail: Run the same alias-write trace with a declaration initializer, a later assignment, and a reassignment.

title: The JSX spread check misses component names that do not start with ASCII capitals.
input: Solid calls `_Editor` in `<_Editor {...state} />`. When the component sets `props.nested.k = 42`, the next read returns `42`, but the card names only the original `10` with no caveat. `Éditeur` fails the same way.
fix: Match Solid's component tag classification for both named props and spreads.
prevent_detail: Check that tags the Solid compiler treats as components trigger the same mutation analysis for named props and spreads.

title: A spread into a local read-only component adds a mutable caveat.
input: `<View {...state} />` where local `View` only returns `props.nested.k` leaves `state.nested.k` at `10`. The base names `10` without a caveat, but this commit adds `mutable` and drops the card's single-producer answer.
fix: Keep the caveat for unresolved components or props that can escape. Skip it when a local component only reads scalar prop values.
prevent_detail: Pair a component-spread fixture that writes a nested prop with one that only reads the same prop.

title: A parenthesized default export hides a write from another module.
input: One module declares `const o = {k: 10}` and uses `export default (o)`. An importer runs `Object.assign(o, {k: 42})`. The exporting module then reads `42`, but both revisions name only `10` with no caveat.
fix: Remove parentheses and type-only wrappers before checking whether a binding is the value of an export assignment.
prevent_detail: Use a two-module mutation fixture to verify that wrapping an exported expression does not remove its caveat.

title: Mermaid warnings point to the wrong line in CRLF fences.
input: In a CRLF Markdown document with one Mermaid fence, a click directive on line 6 reports line 3 and quotes the opening fence. The extracted text uses LF, so the substring search cannot find it in the CRLF source.
fix: Carry the detector’s startLine through sourceType and use startLine minus one as the offset.
prevent_detail: Assert the reported line and text for LF and CRLF fences, including a document that repeats the same diagram text before the fence.

title: /link misclassifies JSON and plain-text media types.
input: A JSON body with Content-Type Application/JSON returns 400, while the same body with application/json returns 200. Plain Draftably sent as text/plain with a profile parameter containing json also returns 400.
fix: Strip media-type parameters, lowercase the type, and match application/json or a supported +json subtype.
prevent_detail: Test media-type dispatch with mixed case, parameters, structured suffixes, and plain-text parameters that contain json.

title: /edit/ redirects when the type option is invalid.
input: With a valid source and ?type=bad, the SVG route returns 400 but /edit/ returns 302 and opens the raw source. The new fallback catches the invalid option as if Mermaid conversion failed.
fix: Validate the type before conversion and fall back to raw source only when the Mermaid importer rejects the diagram.
prevent_detail: Test that edit redirects preserve invalid source for repair but reject invalid route options.

title: The callback caveat confuses setter arguments with stored fields
input: After `setOne("head", "title", rename)`, seeding another store from `one.head` yields a closed answer naming `rename` even though the read holds its return value. Conversely, `setStore({ handler: fn })` gets a callback caveat even though Solid stores `fn` unchanged.
fix: Mark updater invocation at the modeled setter argument, not at the final packed field. Carry that fact through later handoffs, and leave function-valued members of stored objects alone.
prevent_detail: Pair a runtime fixture for an invoked updater whose result seeds another state with one for a function stored unchanged as an object member.

title: The Solid stand-in skips reads after valid selector writes
input: The existing `StorePaths` fixture uses a predicate in `setStore("items", predicate, "label", value)`. The stand-in treats the predicate as a property key and throws before four closed reads. Real Solid completes the write, but the oracle still passes.
fix: Use the installed Solid store implementation or model its selectors faithfully. Report unexpected errors in supported fixture operations instead of silently skipping the reads.
prevent_detail: Compare a selector write with real Solid and assert that the oracle records the reads after the write.

title: A computed-key store write leaves the producer answer closed
input: With `setStore(key, "new")` and a computed key that evaluates to `"title"`, `store.title` holds `"new"`. The base engine discards the unresolved write and reports only `"old"` with no caveat.
fix: Retain unresolved writes that can overlap the field. Keep certainty about the initial value separate from certainty about what the read can hold.
prevent_detail: Check that an unresolved write to a possibly matching key prevents a closed runtime producer answer.

title: A producer value from another invocation can hide a contradiction
input: With a truthy argument, the named initializer produces `"old"` and an unmodeled write makes the read return `"new"`. The no-argument case initializes to `"new"`, so the pooled comparison passes both cases.
fix: Compare each read with producer values from the same execution case, including that case's module initialization.
prevent_detail: Add an oracle self-test where a second invocation produces the value that must fail the first invocation's comparison.

title: A self-reference prevents an exported entry point from running
input: An exported recursive function with no outside caller is excluded because it references itself. Its closed field read recorded no values, even though calling the export reaches the read.
fix: Exclude exports with callers reachable from another fixture entry. Allow explicit drivers where reachability cannot be decided safely.
prevent_detail: Assert that a self-recursive export runs and that an internally supplied helper does not receive an extra synthetic call.

title: Fixture execution can reach real host timers
input: The global denylist blocks `setTimeout` but leaves `AbortSignal.timeout` available. The probe confirmed that fixture code receives Node's real timer function.
fix: Run fixtures in a restricted process and expose only the host APIs they need. Use a controlled clock for timers and enforce a deadline from the parent.
prevent_detail: Give fixture execution an explicit capability allowlist instead of inheriting host globals and shadowing selected names.

title: A save queued during refresh overwrites newer disk changes.
input: Change the caption on disk from Query to Report, then click Done with Mine while the refresh compiles. The queued save sends Mine with the new disk revision. In a separate caption-only save, it also reverted a disk size change from 300×200 to 160×120.
fix: Queue the draft and its opening snapshot instead of two document snapshots. After refresh, rerun the conflict check and apply only the changed fields to the current document.
prevent_detail: Pause a disk refresh, click Done, and verify that replay refuses a conflicting edit and preserves an unrelated disk change.

title: A draft opened during a file switch can write to the destination file.
input: Switch from A to B and open node q while A is still on screen but B is compiling. If both nodes have the same caption, Done writes A's caption edit into B. The draft took its fields from A and its file identity from B. Earlier in the switch, the save URL also changes before the session does, so Done can write to B if the two files are identical.
fix: Finish or cancel the outgoing draft before switching. Block new drafts until the new document is shown, and keep the save URL bound to the session that owns the document.
prevent_detail: Pause a file switch before the session response and again before projection, then verify that editor actions cannot write to the destination from the outgoing drawing.

title: The body comparison uses live file data instead of the opening draft.
input: Edit the body, restore the opening text, and change the caption. If the file changes the body before Done, the editor wrongly refuses the caption. If the file instead changes the body to match a real draft edit, Done can save the caption when it should refuse the whole save. In a tabbed grid, editing and restoring one cell also rewrites the original body even when the file did not change.
fix: Capture immutable opening text and grid values. Compare plain text with the opening text and grid edits with the opening grid in the same representation. Serialize the body only after detecting a net edit.
prevent_detail: Drive the real editor through reverted and matching edits in both text and grid modes, then assert that conflict checks use the opening values.

title: A Table toggle can save different cells from the ones it previews.
input: Open plain code with the rows `col\tval` and `longer\tcontent`, click Table, then click Done without editing a cell. The grid previews `col` and `val` as separate cells, but the saved table shows `col val` in one cell and leaves the next cell empty.
fix: Use the compiler's table reader for a mode-only toggle. If spreadsheet conversion is intentional, make it an explicit body edit that goes through the body conflict check.
prevent_detail: Toggle a tab-separated body to Table without editing cells, then compare the preview grid with the cells from recompiling the saved source.

title: A disk caption change can still block a body-only edit.
input: Open a node titled `" Query "`, leave its caption untouched, and edit the body. If the file changes the caption to `"Report"`, Done compares the untouched draft with the live title, trims it to `Query`, and refuses the save as a caption conflict.
fix: Compare the caption with the immutable title captured at open. Trim only a caption that the user changed.
prevent_detail: Edit only the body of a node whose opening caption has outer spaces, change the caption on disk, and verify that both edits survive.

title: A tab-width change blocks a plain-text body edit.
input: Edit the raw text of a plain code node while the file changes only `tab=4` to `tab=2`. Done refuses the save even though the text box uses raw tabs and the edited body can be read with the new tab width.
fix: Check tab width and table mode as dependencies of edits derived from grid cells. For raw-text edits, compare the raw body and keep the current file options.
prevent_detail: Apply the same disk tab-width change during a plain-text edit and a grid edit, then verify that only the grid edit is refused.

title: Assigning a source ID discards an open table draft.
input: Paste a new table, press Enter before its first compile finishes, and type a caption. When the temporary node ID becomes `table`, the editor remounts and loses the typed caption without a message.
fix: Keep the draft and its opening snapshot under a stable editor token. Update the target ID on remap without replacing the draft.
prevent_detail: Pause projection after creating a node, type into its editor, and verify that assigning the source ID preserves the draft through Done.

title: A later assignment can produce an uncaveated stale value.
input: `let o: {k: number}; o = {k: 10}; const alias = o; alias.k = 42; return o.k` returns `42`, but the graph names only `10` with no caveat. Replacing an earlier initializer fails the same way.
fix: Resolve the binding on the left of a plain assignment and check it for writes and escapes, as for a declaration initializer.
prevent_detail: Run the same alias-write fixture with a declaration initializer, a later assignment, and a reassignment, and compare each trace with the runtime value.

title: Bracket method calls hide writes through `this`.
input: `const o = {k: 10, increment() { ++this.k }}; const key = 'increment'; o[key](); return o.k` returns `11`, but the graph names only `10` with no caveat. A literal bracket key also fails. The dot call adds `mutable`.
fix: Apply the same receiver-write check to element-access and property-access calls.
prevent_detail: Run the same receiver-mutation fixture with dot access, a literal bracket key, and a computed bracket key.

title: Awaiting a fresh promise result marks its container mutable.
input: `const o = {k: 10, done: Promise.resolve({ready: true})}; const {ready} = await o.done; return o.k` returns `10`. The parent leaves the producer uncaveated. This commit adds `mutable` even though the code only reads a scalar from a fresh object.
fix: Keep tracking awaited results that may share state, but do not treat a proven fresh result or a proven scalar-only read as an escape.
prevent_detail: Pair a scalar read from a fresh promise result with a write through a promise that resolves to shared state.

title: Spreading props into a read-only component adds a mutable caveat.
input: `<View {...doc} />` adds `mutable` when local `View` only reads `props.nested.k`. The card loses its single-producer answer even though `doc.nested.k` remains `10`.
fix: Keep the caveat for unresolved components or props that can escape. Skip it when the resolved component only reads scalar fields from plain data.
prevent_detail: Pair a spread into a component that writes a nested prop with a spread into one that only reads the same prop.

title: A wrapped default export hides writes from importers.
input: One module declares `const o = {k: 10}` and uses `export default (o)`. Another module imports it and runs `Object.assign(o, {k: 42})`. A later read in the exporting module returns `42`, but the graph names only `10` with no caveat.
fix: Normalize parentheses and type-only wrappers before checking whether the binding is the value of a default export.
prevent_detail: Use a two-module mutation fixture to check that an export retains its caveat when its expression is wrapped.

title: Per-call comparison rejects valid reads of shared state
input: One export writes `"B"` to a module-level store, then a second export reads it. The engine correctly names `"B"` as a producer, but the oracle rejects the read because the write ran under a different call ID.
fix: Reload modules for independent cases. Put calls that intentionally share state in one explicit scenario and compare values within that scenario.
prevent_detail: Test both a write carried across calls in one scenario and an unrelated call whose value must not count.

title: The Node Solid store hides browser identity changes
input: For `createStore({ head })`, the engine gives a closed answer naming `head` for `store.head`. The Node build returns the original object, so the oracle passes. With the installed browser build, the same probe returns a proxy and fails `Object.is` in all three calls.
fix: Use Solid's browser export for browser fixtures and mark reads that can return a proxy as identity-changing.
prevent_detail: Check object-valued store reads against the library build the app uses, not only against its server build.

title: A setter that accepts either a value or an updater can still get a closed answer
input: With `setStore("title", flag ? update : "fallback")`, the union has no call signature, so the engine names the function-or-string expression without a caveat. Solid calls `update` on the true branch and stores its result. The same rule adds an unnecessary callback caveat when a setter receives a `useRef` object whose `current` field holds a function.
fix: Track possible updater invocation at the modeled setter argument. Carry that fact through later reads and leave stored function members unchanged.
prevent_detail: Pair a setter fixture that alternates between a value and an updater with one that stores a function inside a non-callable object.

title: The React stand-in never checks state after an update
input: A component guarded by `state.title === "old"` queues either an updater or a replacement object. The engine names only `"old"`. The oracle passes because its setter is a no-op, so it sees neither value from the next React render.
fix: Give React state fixtures a driver that applies queued updates and checks the next render.
prevent_detail: Require a React fixture with a queued update to record the field on both sides of the render that applies it.

title: A computed-key store write still leaves the producer answer closed
input: When `key` evaluates to `"title"`, `setStore(key, "new")` changes `store.title` to `"new"`. The engine still names only `"old"` with no caveat because it drops the unresolved write path.
fix: Keep unresolved writes that may overlap the read and attach a caveat without discarding the known initializer.
prevent_detail: Execute a write with a computed key that resolves to the traced field and assert that the answer is not closed.

title: A reference that never calls an export can keep it from running
input: An exported function with a closed field read never runs if the module only stores it in `{ handler: fn }`. Two exports that only call each other are also skipped. Direct self-recursion now runs.
fix: Only suppress a synthetic call when a reachable fixture call drives the export. Allow explicit drivers for registered callbacks and call cycles.
prevent_detail: Check an exported callback stored but never invoked, a mutually recursive pair, and a helper already called by a driver.

title: The recorder silently drops values after 200 observations
input: A fixture read returned `"old"` 200 times, then `"new"` after a write. The recorder kept only `"old"`, dropped the later calls too, and still counted the span as checked.
fix: If a span hits the recording limit, report its check as incomplete instead of passing it.
prevent_detail: Put a contradiction beyond the recording limit and require a failure or an explicit incomplete result.

title: Synchronous fixture code runs without an enforceable deadline
input: `AbortSignal.timeout` is now opaque, but fixture code still runs in the test process with a global denylist. A bounded synchronous loop blocked all three calls past the 50 ms promise wait. That wait starts only after the synchronous code returns.
fix: Run fixtures in a restricted child process with an explicit host API allowlist and a deadline enforced by the parent.
prevent_detail: Enforce execution limits and host access outside the process that runs fixture code.

title: A queued code save overwrites newer disk changes.
input: Change the caption on disk from Query to Report, then click Done with Mine while the refresh compiles. The save sends Mine with the new disk revision. In a separate probe, a caption-only save also reset a disk resize from 300×200 to 160×120.
fix: Queue the draft and its opening snapshot. After projection, check for conflicts again and apply only the fields the user changed.
prevent_detail: Pause a disk refresh, submit a draft, and verify that replay refuses a conflicting edit and preserves unrelated disk changes.

title: A file switch changes the save destination before it changes the drawing.
input: Switch from A to a copy of A named B, then open and save a caption while B's session request is pending. Both file checks still identify A, but the save goes to B. The server accepts it because the copies have the same content revision.
fix: Keep the request URL for the next file separate from the active session's save URL. Use the active session's path and revision for every save.
prevent_detail: Pause navigation before the destination responds and verify that a draft from the outgoing drawing never sends a write to the destination.

title: A failed compile marks the outgoing drawing as the destination file.
input: Open invalid file B from A. A stays visible, but the new check lets a draft open as if it came from B. Repair B on disk with a node that has the same ID and caption. Done writes the caption drafted on A into B, even when their bodies differ.
fix: Set the shown file only when its document projects successfully. Update that identity in the same batch as the projection, including when a disk refresh repairs an invalid file.
prevent_detail: Switch to an invalid file, repair it on disk, and verify that no draft can open from the outgoing drawing under the destination's identity.

title: A Table toggle can discard real cell edits.
input: Open plain code with rows `col\tval` and `longer\tcontent`. Turn on Table, then split the displayed `col val` header into `col` and `val`. Done saves only the mode because the edited cells match a hidden spreadsheet parse, not the grid the user saw. The saved header merges the cells again. Typing and restoring the plain text before toggling also makes the preview disagree with the save.
fix: Compare the draft with the grid the editor actually showed, and detect whether the text changed before choosing how to convert it.
prevent_detail: Drive the real editor through a mode switch with tabs and reverted edits, then compare its final grid with the cells from recompiling the saved source.

title: A disk refresh can make a reverted grid edit block a caption save.
input: Edit a cell, restore it, and change the caption. If the file then changes the column alignment or count, Done refuses the caption. The grid still shares its alignment array with the live document, so the comparison reports a body edit the user did not make.
fix: Copy the opening table's rows and alignment into the draft so a file refresh cannot change the values used to detect user edits.
prevent_detail: Refresh a table's column count or alignment after the user reverts a cell edit, then verify that an independent caption edit still saves.

title: Switching a grid draft to plain text drops its tab-width check.
input: Edit the second row of a tabbed grid at `tab=4`, then turn Table off. If the file changes to `tab=8` before Done, the save writes text made from the old grid. In the probe it replaced the untouched header's tab with a space, even though the newer file read the header as two cells.
fix: Track how the submitted body was made. Check the grid's opening tab width when the body came from cells, even if the editor now shows plain text.
prevent_detail: Apply the same external tab-width change to a typed text draft and to text made from edited cells, then verify that only the latter is refused.

title: Assigning a source ID discards an open table draft.
input: Paste a new table, open its editor before the first compile finishes, and type a caption. When the temporary ID becomes `table`, the editor remounts and the caption disappears without a message.
fix: Key the editor by a stable draft token and update its target node ID when projection assigns the source ID.
prevent_detail: Pause projection after creating a node, edit its draft, and verify that source ID assignment preserves the edit through Done.

title: The oracle accepts values from unrelated calls and future writes
input: A fresh store starts with NEW in the first two calls and OLD in the third. An unmodeled write changes the third store to NEW, but the oracle accepts the value from the first store. A separate probe passed a read using a named write that ran later in the same call.
fix: Isolate independent calls, keep shared-state calls in explicit scenarios, and record a sequence number for each observation so only prior values in that scenario count.
prevent_detail: Require a shared-state write to count while the same value from an unrelated call or a later statement does not.

title: The Solid server build hides object identity changes
input: For createStore({ head }), the engine names head as the only producer of store.head. The oracle passes with the installed server build. The installed browser build returns a proxy that is not Object.is-equal to head.
fix: Run browser fixtures with Solid's browser build and make the engine qualify closed answers when a store read can return a proxy instead of the source object.
prevent_detail: Check object-valued reads against the framework build that the fixture represents.

title: A function typed as Function still bypasses the updater caveat
input: A Solid store field has type Function. Passing const update: Function = () => () => 'NEW' to setStore('title', update) invokes update and stores a different function. The engine names update without a caveat, and all three runtime reads contradict it.
fix: Determine whether the setter may invoke the argument at the modeled updater boundary. Include broad types that can hold a function without exposing a call signature.
prevent_detail: Exercise a runtime updater under both an explicit call signature and a broad static type, and require neither case to name the updater itself as an exact value.

title: Mount-only React effects run again after every update
input: An effect with empty dependencies reads OLD from a store, writes EXTRA through a computed key, and queues a React render. The oracle reruns the effect and reports EXTRA as a contradiction. React does not rerun that effect on the update, so the marked read only observes OLD.
fix: Use a React renderer or make effect scheduling respect dependency arrays and component instances.
prevent_detail: Check that a mount-only effect queues a render without running again, while an effect with changed dependencies does rerun.

title: Unresolved state writes leave producer answers closed
input: A computed Solid store key resolves to title and changes OLD to NEW, but the answer names only OLD. A whole-state write that chooses between an updater and a replacement object also leaves only OLD for React useState, Solid createSignal, and Solid createStore.
fix: Preserve unresolved writes that can overlap the read and mark the answer incomplete while retaining known producers. Do not discard a write because the walk cannot resolve its field or value.
prevent_detail: Execute a computed-key write and a conditional whole-state write, then require neither to leave a closed initializer-only answer.

title: A stored ref's function member gets a callback caveat
input: After setStore('holder', useRef(handler)), the engine adds a callback caveat to holder.current. The setter receives an object and never invokes handler, which the read returns by identity.
fix: Carry updater status from the actual setter argument instead of inferring it from a function-valued field farther along the producer path.
prevent_detail: Pair a callable setter argument with a non-callable argument that contains a function, including an object returned by a modeled call.

title: An unreachable caller can exclude an export from the oracle
input: Two exported functions call each other only behind a guard that is false for their default arguments. Either can run on its own, but each syntactic call excludes the other export, so neither closed read runs. An export merely stored in an object now runs.
fix: Skip synthetic calls only when a reachable scenario drives the export, and declare drivers for callback and call-cycle cases.
prevent_detail: Require a runnable export to be observed when its only callers are unreachable or in an otherwise undriven cycle.

title: Fixture code can block the test worker without a deadline
input: A 90 ms synchronous loop completed in each of the three calls despite the 50 ms promise wait. The call runs before the wait starts, so a nonterminating fixture can hold the worker. The in-process global denylist is also not a host-access boundary.
fix: Execute fixtures in a restricted worker with an explicit host API allowlist and a deadline enforced by the parent.
prevent_detail: Enforce execution time and host access outside the process that runs fixture code.

title: Writes to unrelated store fields make the read look uncertain.
input: After `setStore("other", 1)`, `store.title` still reads `"FIRST"`, but its producer now carries a `write` caveat. The same happens for nested sibling paths and for `setStore({ other: 1 })`. This accounts for five of the six lost closed answers in the existing fixtures.
fix: Skip writes whose known path or merge keys exclude the read. Keep the caveat for unknown keys and for whole-value replacements that omit the field.
prevent_detail: Pair a known-disjoint write that must preserve a closed answer with an unknown-key write and a whole-value replacement that must not.

title: A store updater is listed as the stored value while the card still says only one producer was found.
input: With `k` initialized to `"OLD"`, `setStore("k", s => s + "NEW")` makes the read return `"OLDNEW"`. The engine lists the updater function as the later value and puts the callback caveat only on that entry. The card still reports `"OLD"` as the only producer found.
fix: Follow the modeled updater return instead of recording the function as a value. When a later write remains unresolved, propagate its caveat to the whole answer.
prevent_detail: Run inline and named updaters and compare their stored results with the producer values and the card's certainty.

title: A write through an alias of the state object disappears from a fresh read.
input: After `const alias = doc()` and `alias.k = "NEW"`, a fresh `doc().k` reads `"NEW"` but reports only `"OLD"` with no caveat. Passing `doc()` to a mutating helper has the same result. The probe also reproduced the alias case with a React state object.
fix: Track writes and escapes of the object returned by a state read across its aliases. Caveat the state's producers when the object can change and the write cannot be traced.
prevent_detail: Run a fixture that mutates a state object through one read and checks the producer answer at a separate read.

title: A setter passed through an options object can write state without any warning.
input: Pass a signal setter as `touch({ set })` to a helper that destructures `set` and calls `set({ k: "NEW" })`. The getter reads `"NEW"`, but its only producer is still `"OLD"` with no caveat. A setter called through `set.bind(null)` also disappears.
fix: Carry the setter's state identity through resolved argument fields and bound calls. Mark an unresolved setter escape as a possible write to that state.
prevent_detail: Compare a direct setter call with the same call through a holder object, a destructured parameter, and a bound function.

title: A computed store path can turn a descendant write into a false producer for its parent.
input: With `key` equal to `"k"`, `setStore("doc", key, { k: "NEW" })` can replace a string at `store.doc.k` with an object. The engine drops the computed segment and names the string `"NEW"` inside that object as the later producer for `store.doc.k`. Neither named producer equals the value read, and the answer stays closed.
fix: Keep an unknown suffix on the write path. Use the known prefix to rule out siblings, but do not treat the leaf as a replacement for any value above the unknown segment.
prevent_detail: Check writes with a literal prefix and computed suffix at a parent read, the matching leaf read, and a disjoint sibling read.

title: An assignment counts as a mutation of the object it creates.
input: `let o: { k: string }` followed by `o = { k: "OLD" }` and `return o.k` now gives `"OLD"` a `mutable` caveat. The binding scan finds the same assignment that installed the object. Replacing an earlier literal with a new literal produces the same false caveat on the new value.
fix: Exclude the assignment that installs this producer from its mutation scan. Keep checks for other writes and escapes.
prevent_detail: Require declaration initialization and later initialization to agree when the object does not escape, then add an alias write that makes both answers uncertain.

title: Several later assignments still miss alias mutation.
input: Assign `o = { k: "OLD" }` after `let { o } = initial`, then write `"NEW"` through an alias. The read reports only `"OLD"` without a caveat on both revisions. I reproduced the same result with a non-null wrapper on the right side and with `o ??= { k: "OLD" }`. A plain parameter reassignment now gets the caveat. A standalone `[o] = [{ k: "OLD" }]` target stayed open without a producer.
fix: Resolve the assigned value's destination through the same binding and wrapper rules used by the assignment collector. Leave the answer open when that destination cannot be checked.
prevent_detail: Run the same alias mutation after direct, wrapped, conditional, and destructured assignments and assert that none produces a false closed answer.

title: A default-exported child object can change without a caveat.
input: `export default (o.doc)` hands out the same object that a local `o.doc.k` reads. An importer calling `Object.assign(doc, { k: "NEW" })` changes that read, but the card still names only `"OLD"`. The export check runs before the host follows the access chain from `o` to `o.doc`.
fix: Check for a default export after following the access chain and its wrappers.
prevent_detail: Run an importer mutation against both a wrapped binding export and a wrapped child-object export.

title: A pending save can silently drop the next file’s edit.
input: While B is opening, save a caption in A and delay its PUT response. After B opens, save a caption in B. Only A gets a PUT, but B shows Saved. A disk event buffered during A’s PUT can also replace B’s drawing.
fix: Give each file session its own save queue and buffered disk events. A response for A must neither consume B’s pending save nor apply A’s disk events to B.
prevent_detail: Hold a PUT across a file switch, then verify that both edits reach their own files and that buffered events stay with their originating session.

title: A queued inline label can overwrite a disk change.
input: Edit a node label while an external edit changes the same label. Finish the inline edit while the refresh compiles. The viewer sends the local label with the refreshed disk revision, so the revision check accepts the overwrite.
fix: Queue a label patch with its opening value and validate it against the refreshed label before writing.
prevent_detail: Pause a disk refresh while saving each inline draft and verify that same-field changes are refused while unrelated changes survive.

title: Saving during a Source panel compile can lose the Code edit.
input: Add a size line in the Source panel, then open Code and save a caption before the source compile finishes. The command runs against the new drawing but translates against the old source. The Source panel then saves its unmerged text. The canvas shows the new caption even though the saved source has the old one.
fix: Run queued commands only after the caller has committed the source and history that match the projected drawing.
prevent_detail: Queue a Code save during Source panel compilation and assert that the final saved text, drawn node, and undo history agree.

title: A superseded file open still reloads the older file.
input: Open B, then open C before B responds. C opens first. B then returns false, which go() treats as a missing file and uses to reload the page at B.
fix: Distinguish a superseded open from a missing file. Only the latest navigation may reload, update history, or start listening.
prevent_detail: Resolve two navigation requests in reverse order and verify that only the latest changes the URL, drawing, or event stream.

title: A superseding redraw can strand a queued draft on its temporary ID.
input: Paste a table and open its editor. While the paste compiles, refresh the source with an unrelated comment and save the caption. The refresh supersedes the compile that would deliver the ID map. The table is still there, but the save says it was removed or renamed.
fix: Keep pending ID maps with the file session and apply them on the first successful projection that contains the assigned source IDs.
prevent_detail: Supersede a paste projection before it publishes its ID map and verify that both open and queued drafts follow the saved node.

title: An unexpected compile error strands later Code saves.
input: Queue a caption save while a refresh compiles a code block with 140,000 short lines. Compilation throws a RangeError. The queue is not cleared, and another Done press queues behind it even though compilation has stopped. Neither save gets a result.
fix: Report unexpected compile failures and explicitly refuse waiting commands. Do not leave them queued against a drawing that does not match the current source.
prevent_detail: Make compilation reject with a non-DSL error and verify that queued saves get a visible refusal and later saves can run after recovery.

title: Reverting a text edit in the grid still counts as a body edit.
input: Change a word in a tab-separated code block, turn on Table, then restore the original word in its cell. The grid matches the opening body, but Done still sends a body patch. If the file changed a different cell, this wrongly refuses the Table switch.
fix: Keep a separate baseline for how the opening body reads as a grid. Compare the final grid with that baseline even when the user entered Table mode from edited text.
prevent_detail: Revert an edit in a different editor mode and verify that saving another field keeps a concurrent change to the reverted field.

title: Timeline rows and links stay on screen after an edit removes them.
input: Rename a dated row, then delete it. The first drawing keeps the old title after the rename. After deletion, it still draws the row and its dependency, and placedItems still reports the dependency even though the graph no longer has it.
fix: Apply the affected timeline plans from the checked source before starting the async redraw. Map their IDs to the optimistic document and preserve the current timeline origin.
prevent_detail: For timeline rename and delete actions, compare rendered text, rendered IDs, and geometry immediately after commit and after the saved source recompiles.

title: A timeline edge that shares a node ID inherits the node's viewer behavior.
input: Use `edge deploy deploy -> test "Dependency"` in a timeline with a `deploy` row. A click dispatched on the edge path emits node activation, and registering `body:deploy` marks the dependency label as node body text, which the viewer hides at full detail.
fix: Tag timeline edges with their item kind. Match marks by ID and kind for activation and outline navigation, and exclude edge marks when applying node body slots.
prevent_detail: Mount the viewer with a node and an edge that share a legal ID, then verify activation, outline navigation, and body-slot styling independently.

title: The inferred-edge guard misses changes in which panel shows an edge.
input: In a comparison, delete a `+edge` that overrides a table row's `->` line. The inferred edge keeps its ID, so the new guard permits the save. The immediate drawing still marks it as removed, but the saved file draws it in both panels. A `-edge` override has the inverse mismatch.
fix: Apply the checked inferred edge's status to the optimistic edge when its ID is unchanged, or refuse the edit if that change is unsupported.
prevent_detail: Round-trip deletion of added and removed table overrides and compare edge membership in each panel, not just the set of edge IDs.

title: Adding a written table connection briefly draws two lines where the file draws one.
input: Use Connect between two table rows that already have an inferred `->` line. The immediate SVG shows both the existing crow's-foot line and the new arrow. The saved source draws only the arrow because the written edge replaces the inferred line.
fix: Remove the superseded inferred edge from the optimistic document once the checked source confirms the replacement.
prevent_detail: Include Connect between existing endpoints in the edit matrix and compare the rendered edge count and markers before and after recompilation.

title: A field mismatch hides a whole-state replacement.
input: For a signal seeded with `{ k: 'OLD' }`, conditionally call `set({ k: replacement.other })`, then always call `set(replacement)` where `replacement` is `{ other: 'NEW' }`. The read returns `undefined`, but both named producers have no caveat. The sibling read keeps the `other` edge in the slice, so `elsewhere` suppresses the stop for the replacement. Round 1 kept the caveat.
fix: Skip a mismatched field only when the write is known to preserve that field. A whole-value replacement that omits it must keep the caveat.
prevent_detail: Run the same replacement with and without a second path that reads a sibling field, and require both answers to stay uncertain.

title: A callable updater can lose its write caveat without a traced return.
input: Pass `actions.rename` to a signal setter, where `rename` returns `{ k: previous.k + 'NEW' }`. The read returns `OLDNEW`, but the graph and card report only `'OLD'` with no caveat. Round 1 kept the write caveat.
fix: Skip the updater value only when the same setter call has a modeled return path. Callability alone does not show that the return was traced.
prevent_detail: Compare direct and member-access updaters at runtime, and require either the returned value or a caveat for each call.

title: Disjoint Solid store merges still reduce certainty.
input: With `createStore({ k: 'OLD', other: 0 })`, `set({ other: 1 })` leaves `s.k` at `OLD` but adds a `write` caveat. The same happens with `set('doc', { other: 1 })` when `doc` is a plain object and the read is `s.doc.k`. Literal sibling paths now stay closed.
fix: Carry merge semantics to the producer walk. Skip a patch only when its known keys exclude the read and the write merges at that level.
prevent_detail: Pair disjoint top-level and nested merges with replacements that omit the same field, and check that only the replacements lose certainty.

title: A store path updater is shown as the value it writes.
input: `set('k', v => v + 'NEW')` makes a field initialized to `OLD` read `OLDNEW`. The card lists the updater function as the later value and still marks `'OLD'` as the only producer found. The callback caveat stays on the later entry.
fix: Follow the modeled updater return before recording the producer. If the return cannot be traced, put the write caveat on the whole answer.
prevent_detail: Run inline and named path updaters and compare their stored values with the graph's producers and the card's certainty.

title: A state object mutation through an alias disappears from a fresh read.
input: After `const alias = doc()` and `alias.k = 'NEW'`, a fresh `doc().k` returns `NEW` but reports only `'OLD'` without a caveat. Passing `doc()` to a helper that mutates it gives the same result.
fix: Track aliases and escapes of the object a state read returns. Caveat later reads of that state when the mutation cannot be traced.
prevent_detail: Mutate the object through one state read and check the producer answer at a separate read of the same state.

title: A setter loses its state identity when passed through an object.
input: Pass `set` as `invoke({ set })` to a helper that destructures and invokes it with `{ k: 'NEW' }`. The read returns `NEW` but reports only `'OLD'` without a caveat. Calling the setter through `set.bind(null)` also loses the write.
fix: Preserve setter identity through resolved fields, arguments, and bound calls. Record an unresolved setter escape as a possible write.
prevent_detail: Compare a direct setter call with the same write through an options object, a destructured parameter, and a bound function.

title: A store path drops its computed suffix and invents a producer.
input: With `key` equal to `'k'`, `set('doc', key, { k: 'NEW' })` makes `s.doc.k` hold the object `{ k: 'NEW' }`. The graph instead names the old string and the new object's inner string as producers, with no caveats.
fix: Keep an unknown suffix after the last literal key. Use the known prefix to exclude siblings, not to treat the write as a replacement at the prefix.
prevent_detail: Check a literal-prefix write with a computed suffix at its parent, matching leaf, and disjoint sibling.

title: Ignoring the installing assignment also hides escapes of its result.
input: `Object.assign(o = { k: 'OLD' }, { k: 'NEW' })` makes `o.k` return `NEW`. Round 2 reports only `'OLD'` without a caveat, while round 1 caveated it. Chained assignment to an alias also reproduces the loss.
fix: Ignore the binding write itself, but check whether the enclosing expression exposes the assigned object.
prevent_detail: Pair a standalone assignment with the same assignment used as an argument or alias initializer, and require uncertainty only when the object can escape.

title: Later assignments can still bypass the binding mutation scan.
input: Assign `{ k: 'OLD' }` to `o`, then change `o.k` through an alias. The read returns `NEW` but reports only `'OLD'` when `o` came from `let { o } = initial`, when the right side is `({ k: 'OLD' })!`, or when an uninitialized `o` is assigned with `??=`. A standalone `[o] = [...]` stayed open.
fix: Use the assignment collector's wrapper and target rules to resolve the destination, including binding elements and logical assignments. Leave the answer open if the destination cannot be checked.
prevent_detail: Run the same alias mutation after plain, wrapped, logical, and destructured-binding assignments and reject false closed answers.

title: A default-exported child object can change without a caveat.
input: `export default (o.doc)` shares the object behind `o.doc.k`. When an importer changes `doc.k` to `NEW`, the local read still reports only `'OLD'` without a caveat. Exporting the wrapped binding itself is now caught.
fix: Check for a default export after following the member access chain and its wrappers.
prevent_detail: Run an importer mutation against both a wrapped root export and a wrapped child export, then check the original module's read.

title: The new midpoint can put a label beneath a crossing edge.
input: In a pinned diagram, a horizontal `AI` arrow runs from (100, 140) to (149, 140), and a vertical arrow crosses at x=124.5. The base puts the label clear of both lines. The new midpoint fits between the boxes, so placement skips that fallback and the SVG paints the vertical line and its halo over the text. The new unit test checks attachment and box clearance in an empty gap.
fix: Try the shifted placement when every on-route candidate crosses another edge through the text. Prefer the shifted placement if it keeps the text clear.
prevent_detail: Render a narrow-gap fixture with and without a crossing edge, then assert that the clear gap keeps the label attached and the crossing stays out of the text.

title: Tight labels can clip the default arrowhead.
input: A 49 px gap centers a 41 px `Pass` label and leaves 4 px before the arrow tip. Rasterizing the SVG confirms that the label background cuts off both arrowhead wings. The base already allows the same overlap with `Wait` in a 48 px gap.
fix: Include the painted bounds of the default arrowhead when checking clearance for tight labels.
prevent_detail: Check that the label background clears the painted arrowhead when the gap is only a few pixels wider than the label.

title: A queued inline label can overwrite another file.
input: Edit a label in A while a disk refresh is compiling, then navigate to B with the same object ID and opening label. Navigation queues the edit, and B's projection runs it. The PUT writes A's label to B.
fix: Capture the opening file session with the inline draft and check both the active and drawn sessions before applying it, as the Code editor does.
prevent_detail: Queue each draft type across a file switch between copies and assert that it never sends a PUT to the other file.

title: The save restart can drop an edit and report it as saved.
input: While B is opening, hold A's first PUT and finish a second edit in A. When B opens and the PUT resolves, the second A edit is lost. The restart sends unedited B and shows a Saved toast. If A's PUT rejects instead, a pending B edit never gets a PUT.
fix: Give each file its own pending source and save state. Finish or report A's pending work and let B save independently of A's response.
prevent_detail: Hold a PUT across a file switch, queue edits on both sides, and verify request paths, bodies, and status for both a successful and a rejected response.

title: A conflict from one file can replace another file.
input: Get a save conflict in A, then open B. The conflict banner remains, now under B's name. Clicking “Save my edit over it” sends A's entire proposal with B's revision and replaces B.
fix: Bind the conflict proposal to its file session and expose or apply it only in that session.
prevent_detail: Open another file with an unresolved conflict and verify that no conflict action can write the old proposal to it.

title: Reverting Source text during layout strands later saves.
input: Add a size line in Source, then revert to the original text before layout finishes. The revert returns without canceling the compile. The canvas draws the reverted size line, the committed source never changes, and Code saves close without writing. A later disk redraw can replay the first queued save.
fix: Supersede the pending projection when the user reverts to committed text. Drain commands only after that text is drawn again.
prevent_detail: Hold a Source compile, revert to the committed text, and verify that the drawing, saved text, and queued commands all follow the revert.

title: An older navigation can still undo the latest choice.
input: Hold B's open, then open C. If B returns 404 or its request fails, the page reloads at B. If the newer action is Back to the current file or Start, even a successful B response takes over because neither action supersedes the pending open.
fix: Issue a navigation ticket for every destination, including the current file and Start. Check it before starting a session, reloading, or updating the URL.
prevent_detail: Resolve a held open after a newer navigation to a file, the current file, or Start, and verify that neither success nor failure changes the chosen view.

title: A compile failure silently queues later saves.
input: Refresh to a code block large enough to throw a RangeError, with no save waiting. After layout stops, press Done on a caption edit. The editor closes without a write or refusal. A later valid refresh applies that old edit.
fix: Record the failed revision as blocked. Refuse later commands immediately until a valid revision draws, and release drafts when refusing them.
prevent_detail: Test commands submitted both before and after a compiler rejection, then verify that recovery does not replay refused commands.

title: A shifted legend row can receive another row's label.
input: Edit the first of two legend rows with the same label but different colors. If a refresh deletes the first row, the second moves to its index and passes the opening-value check. The save renames the wrong row.
fix: Use row identity as well as the opening label. Refuse the edit if the latest list no longer identifies the original row unambiguously.
prevent_detail: Delete or reorder one of two same-label rows during a draft and assert that the save never modifies the other row.

title: A delayed text removal clears a newer selection.
input: Empty a note or legend row while a refresh compiles, then select the diagram title before the queued removal runs. The removal and undo both work, but the removal clears the title selection.
fix: After a successful removal, adjust selection only if it points at the removed row or at a row whose index changed.
prevent_detail: Change selection while a text removal waits and verify that the completed removal preserves any unaffected selection.

title: A crossing halo can erase part of a midpoint label.
input: A 49 px arrow from (100, 140) to (149, 140) puts `Pass` at (124.5, 140). A vertical edge at x=112 just clears the text check, but its 8 px halo erases part of the P in the rendered SVG. The base places the label clear of the crossing. The new test checks a centerline through the middle and misses this case.
fix: Reject a new midpoint when another edge’s painted stroke or crossing halo overlaps the text.
prevent_detail: Render a narrow-gap fixture with a crossing just outside the text bounds and assert that the painted halo leaves the glyphs clear.

title: Tight labels still clip the default arrowhead.
input: In round two, a 49 px gap centers a 41 px `Pass` label with 4 px before the arrow tip. The SVG label background clips both wings. The same overlap reproduces on the base with `Wait` in a 48 px gap.
fix: Include the painted bounds of the default arrowhead when checking clearance for tight labels.
prevent_detail: Render labels in gaps only a few pixels wider than their boxes and assert that both arrowhead wings remain visible.

title: A distant parallel arrow vetoes a clear standoff move
input: In a four-box diagram, the main arrow runs at x=253 beside a box whose right edge is x=240. A separate vertical arrow at x=480 blocks the move to x=260 even though that move adds no crossing or lane conflict. Removing the distant arrow restores the full 20 px standoff. Reproduced through both the .draft compiler and public graph API.
fix: Use the shared-gap veto only for bounded gaps. For open-space moves, check the proposed path for crossings and reduced lane spacing.
prevent_detail: Add a routing test that places an unrelated parallel arrow beyond the requested lane gap and asserts that the original arrow still reaches its standoff.

title: The clearance pass changes the route with facing disabled
input: With facing=false, the existing own-standoff fixture expects the arrow to turn 13 px from the source box. The pinned commit turns at 20 px and fails tests/routing-own-standoff.test.ts:28. The later commit fb053fc2 restores the expected behavior.
fix: Gate the open-space standoff move on facingFans.
prevent_detail: Run the existing facing=false regression test against the exact commit whenever a routing pass changes own-box standoff.

title: A clearance slide can make a route cross itself
input: In a direct pass probe with standoff=40, a box ends at x=100 and the route follows (220,150), (130,150), (130,100), (110,100), (110,240), (220,240). Sliding the x=110 run to x=140 reverses the connecting leg at y=100 and creates a self-crossing at (140,150). The pass accepts it.
fix: Reject a slide that reverses a connecting leg or introduces a self-intersection.
prevent_detail: Test that sliding a segment past an adjacent bend cannot turn a simple orthogonal path into a self-intersecting path.

title: A return elsewhere in the slice can hide an unresolved updater write.
input: Conditionally call `set(actions.rename({ k: 'PREVIEW' }))`, then pass `actions.rename` itself to `set`. The preview call's return suppresses the caveat for the updater call. When `Object.assign` has replaced `rename`, the read returns `OLDTWO`, but the card shows a sure initial producer and lists only the original function's expression as a later write. An inline updater that falls through also leaves the initial producer uncaveated.
fix: Skip the updater argument only when the same setter call has a traced result that covers every exit. Apply unresolved return caveats to the whole answer.
prevent_detail: Run an updater through both a direct call and a setter, and check that neither the direct call nor one traced branch can hide an unresolved setter result.

title: Disjoint Solid store merges still make a sure field uncertain.
input: `set({ other: 1 })` leaves `s.k` at `OLD` but adds a write caveat. So does `set('doc', { other: 1 })` when `doc` is a plain object and the read is `s.doc.k`. The equivalent literal sibling path `set('doc', 'other', 1)` stays closed.
fix: Carry merge semantics into the producer walk. Keep the answer closed only when the operation merges at that level and its known keys exclude the read field.
prevent_detail: Pair disjoint merges with replacements that omit the same field, and assert that only the replacements lose certainty.

title: A store path updater is shown as the value it writes.
input: `set('k', v => v + 'NEW')` changes `s.k` from `OLD` to `OLDNEW`. The card lists the function as the later value. Its callback caveat stays on the later entry, so the initial answer still appears sure.
fix: Follow the updater result before naming a producer. If the result cannot be traced, apply a write caveat to the whole answer.
prevent_detail: Run inline and named path updaters and compare the stored value with the producer and certainty shown on the card.

title: A write through a signal value alias disappears from a fresh read.
input: After `const alias = doc()` and `alias.k = 'NEW'`, a fresh `doc().k` returns `NEW` but reports only `OLD` with no caveat.
fix: Associate aliases and escapes of getter results with the state they came from. Caveat a fresh read when that state has an unresolved mutation.
prevent_detail: Mutate a state object through one getter result and check the producer answer at a separate call of the same getter.

title: Object and bound aliases can hide a setter write.
input: `invoke({ set })` can destructure and call the setter with `{ k: 'NEW' }`. A `set.bind(null)` alias can do the same. Both reads return `NEW` but report only `OLD` with no caveat.
fix: Preserve state identity through resolved object fields and bound functions. Record an unresolved setter escape as a possible write.
prevent_detail: Compare direct setter calls with identical writes through an options object, a destructured parameter, and a bound function.

title: Dropping a computed store key invents a later producer.
input: With `key` equal to `'k'`, `set('doc', key, { k: 'NEW' })` makes `s.doc.k` hold the object `{ k: 'NEW' }`. The closed answer instead names the initial string and the string inside the new object.
fix: Keep the unknown suffix after the literal path prefix. Use the prefix to exclude siblings, but do not treat the write as a replacement at that prefix.
prevent_detail: Check a write with a literal prefix and computed suffix at its parent, matching leaf, and disjoint sibling.

title: A zero-argument Solid setter clears state without recording a write.
input: For `createSignal<{ k: string } | undefined>({ k: 'OLD' })`, `set()` is valid and makes `doc()?.k` return `undefined`. The card reports only `OLD` with no caveat because the collector emits no write edge.
fix: Record a zero-argument Solid signal setter call as a write of `undefined`.
prevent_detail: Compare omitted and explicit undefined values for state setters whose signatures allow either form.

title: Several later assignments still bypass the mutation scan.
input: Alias mutation after installing `{ k: 'OLD' }` still leaves a false closed answer when the binding came from `let { o } = initial`, the right side uses `!`, or the assignment uses `??=`. Plain identifier reassignment and parameter assignment did not leave false closed answers. The tested `[o] = [...]` target stayed open.
fix: Use the assignment collector's target and wrapper rules to find the binding. Keep the answer open if the producer walk cannot check the destination.
prevent_detail: Run the same alias mutation after plain, wrapped, logical, and destructured assignments and reject any false closed answer.

title: A default-exported child object can change without a caveat.
input: `export default (o.doc)` hands the child object to an importer. Its `Object.assign(doc, { k: 'NEW' })` changes the original module's `o.doc.k` to `NEW`, but the card reports only `OLD` with no caveat.
fix: Check for a default export after following the member access chain and its wrappers.
prevent_detail: Mutate wrapped root and child exports through an importer, then check both reads in the exporting module.

title: Switching files discards a Code edit after its PUT fails.
input: Hold A's first PUT, request B, then finish a second Code edit in A. Let the first PUT succeed and return HTTP 500 for the second. B opens and removes A's retry banner. Reopening A shows only the first edit.
fix: Check the save outcome before calling begin. Keep A open with its pending text and Retry action if the write failed.
prevent_detail: Hold a file switch across successive PUTs and verify that a failed write leaves its text available for retry in the original file.

title: A label opened on the previous drawing can write to the next file.
input: Open invalid B from valid A. While A's drawing remains visible, start editing its Alpha label. Repair B with a node that has the same ID and label, then finish the edit. The viewer sends A's label to B and reports it saved. The stack base also does this.
fix: Match the drawn and active sessions before opening an inline draft, as the Code editor does. Check both again before writing.
prevent_detail: Keep the old drawing visible through an invalid file open and verify that no draft started on it can write to the new file after recovery.

title: A temporary ID can retarget a pasted table's draft to another table.
input: Paste a table in an embedded editor and open its Code draft before projection. Have the host replace the source with a different untitled table that also uses the ID `table`. After that source draws, save a caption. The host receives the caption on its replacement table. The stack base refuses this save.
fix: Tie each temporary ID map to the revision that created the node. Carry it forward only while the new revision still contains that creation.
prevent_detail: Replace an optimistic creation before projection with a different object that uses its assigned ID and verify that its draft cannot write to the replacement.

title: Reverting Source text after a compile exception leaves draft saves blocked.
input: Paste an oversized code body into Source to trigger a RangeError, then revert to the committed text. The valid drawing is already visible, so the revert does not redraw it. Code and label saves keep saying the file could not be drawn.
fix: On revert, redraw the committed revision if the last compile failed. Track the failure on the revision that failed.
prevent_detail: Force an unexpected compile failure, revert to the already drawn source, and verify that the next draft saves without another source edit.

title: An open inline edit can reverse the order of queued Code saves.
input: During a slow refresh, finish two caption drafts on the same node, then start editing another node's label. The first Code command's transaction finishes that label and reenters the queue. The PUTs write `Second` and then `First`. The second draft should have been refused after the first changed its opening value.
fix: Make the queue drain non-reentrant. Append commands submitted by a running transaction and validate each command immediately before applying it.
prevent_detail: Submit another command from a transaction hook and assert that queued writes keep their submission order and recheck their opening values.

title: An invalid Source draft can leave a closed Code edit queued until a later refresh.
input: Finish a caption edit during a disk refresh, then let invalid Source text supersede that compile. The error ends compilation, but the drawing and committed source differ, so the queue does not drain. A later valid refresh saves the old caption without another Done.
fix: Reject and release waiting drafts on the terminal compile error instead of passing them through the successful-projection check.
prevent_detail: Supersede a pending refresh with invalid Source text and verify that waiting commands receive a refusal and cannot replay on recovery.

title: A midpoint label can hide the turn of another arrow.
input: Two arrows leave the same diamond tip at (100, 140). The labeled arrow runs 49 px to the right, and the other turns up at (124.5, 140). The new AI label covers the turn in the SVG. The base leaves the turn visible. The audit also skips edges that share a start point.
fix: Exempt only the shared portion of the two paths from clearance checks. Check the branch after it leaves that portion.
prevent_detail: Render a fork with a label near its split and assert that both branches remain visible.

title: The halo regression test passes with the halo fix removed.
input: The pinned code clears both original crossings, but the new test still passes with the round-two code. The Pass label center is 12.5 px from the crossing, which exceeds half the 21 px label height even when the halo covers the left edge of the text.
fix: Assert that the painted halo stays clear of the text in the rendered fixture.
prevent_detail: Run each rendering regression test against the commit that still has the defect and verify that it fails.

title: Tight labels still clip the default arrowhead.
input: A 41 px Pass label in a 49 px gap leaves 4 px to the arrow tip. The label background clips both wings of the 6 px chevron in the SVG. The same defect occurs on the base with Wait in a 48 px gap.
fix: Include the painted bounds of the default arrowhead when checking label clearance.
prevent_detail: Render a labeled arrow in a tight gap and assert that both arrowhead wings remain visible.

title: A recovered lane can block a later route in quick mode
input: In the Exploreda population fixture `exploreda-9c5c3daeaf/v0.draft`, quick mode recovers `edge_11` and changes the path chosen for `edge_6`. That path makes the search for `edge_7` fail. The preview draws `edge_7` along the Crossfilter box outline and drops its configured target offset from 16 to 0. The base routes `edge_7` cleanly, and the full pass still clears it.
fix: Defer generated-lane retries until after the initial routing pass. Retry only blocked lanes against the routes already found. An in-memory probe of this order cleared all three initially blocked lanes and kept `edge_7` clear.
prevent_detail: Run quick routing over the audit corpus and assert that a fallback for one edge never turns an initially clear edge into a blocked stand-in.

title: The Compare worker bypasses generated lanes
input: Open `hn-deploy/v0.draft` in Compare. The Current card routes `d6` from the left of `pkg`, while the editor uses the generated lane and leaves from the bottom. The same input builder omits lane bends and their retry metadata for all source candidates. Compare and the editor drew different lane paths in 69 of 73 files with generated lanes, on both the base and reviewed commit.
fix: Use the scene worker's route-input builder for source comparison candidates so both paths expand lanes and route with the same constraints.
prevent_detail: Compile each audit file through the scene and Current comparison tasks and assert that route points, ports and blocked states agree.

title: Label placement can remove a bend that the retry retained
input: For a long-labelled edge between boxes at `(0,0,110,55)` and `(73,153,84,59)` with lane `{y:82, leave:158}`, the retry returns a clear route through the retained bend `(158,82)`. The label-spacing pass moves the run to `y=74`, so the drawn line misses that bend in both quick and full modes.
fix: Carry the retained waypoint constraints with the recovered route and reject label-spacing moves that leave those constraints.
prevent_detail: Assert that the final drawn polyline still passes through the retained waypoints of a recovered lane with a long label.

title: Dropping both bends can miss a clear route that needs one
input: With endpoint boxes `(0,0,110,55)` and `(80,150,80,60)`, a third box at `(-20,95,60,55)`, and lane `{y:83, enter:52}`, quick and full routing return a blocked stand-in. Dropping only the first generated bend yields a clear route through the inner point and the original exit bend with the same bottom and left ports.
fix: When the retry with both outer bends removed still fails, try removing each outer bend on its own. Keep the inner waypoints and port settings in each attempt.
prevent_detail: Test a generated lane where a one-end retry succeeds and a two-end retry fails, and verify that the clear route preserves the inner point and ports.

title: A clearance slide lengthens an existing lane conflict
input: In the held-out chess practice diagram, the slide moves m11 from x=597 to x=604. Its overlap with m9 at 6 px separation grows from 3 px to 10 px. The lane deficit rises from 1.88 to 6.25, while the lane-pair count stays at one.
fix: Compare lane deficit as well as lane-pair count for the complete candidate path, including both legs that change length.
prevent_detail: Check that a clearance slide cannot lengthen an existing overlap below the requested edge gap.

title: Moving away from a box can extend a run along a group border
input: With standoff=40, a top-to-top edge from a group member to an outside box shifts its horizontal run from y=187 to y=160. Its next leg now runs for 170 px within 2 px of the group's right border, up from 143 px.
fix: Check group-border clearance on the resized legs and reject a slide that lengthens an existing close run along a border.
prevent_detail: Route an edge from a member to an outside box and assert that a clearance slide cannot extend the run along the inside of the frame.

title: A slide can cross an earlier segment without reversing either adjacent leg
input: In a direct pass probe with standoff=40, the route follows (200,140), (130,140), (130,70), (60,70), (60,100), (110,100), (110,240), (240,240). Moving the x=110 run to x=140 preserves both adjacent leg directions but crosses the first segment at (140,140).
fix: Check the three modified segments against nonadjacent segments of the same route before accepting the slide.
prevent_detail: Assert that the clearance pass preserves a simple path when the proposed slide passes an earlier segment without reversing either adjacent leg.

title: Source Compare bypasses generated lanes.
input: In `hn-deploy/v0.draft`, Compare routes `d6` from the left of `pkg` while the editor routes it from the bottom. I reproduced the mismatch at both requested commits and verified that the later commit `8a980c14` resolves it on this fixture.
fix: Use the scene worker's route-input builder for source comparison candidates.
prevent_detail: Run scene and Current comparison tasks over the same source corpus and assert that route points, ports, and blocked states agree.

title: Retries for an unreachable lane slow down dragging.
input: In `srcly-scan-lifecycle/v0.draft`, every retry for `dispatch` keeps an inner waypoint beyond the group's left wall. The edge stays blocked. Moving the cache node through 15 measured drag frames raised median quick routing time from 22 ms to 86 ms.
fix: Skip a search when a required waypoint is strictly inside an obstacle that the current candidate cannot cross. An in-memory guard kept the reviewed routes identical and reduced the median to 12 ms.
prevent_detail: Check that retries with a required waypoint inside an impassable obstacle exit before grid search and preserve the blocked result.

title: Compare expands collapsed groups on the Current card.
input: Collapse the `source` group in `hn-deploy/v0.draft` and open Compare. The editor starts edge `d6` at the collapsed group, while the Current card starts it at the hidden `pkg` node. Five routes differ. This also occurs on the base commit.
fix: Capture the editor view when Compare opens and pass it to the shared scene projection for every source candidate.
prevent_detail: Compare the card and editor route endpoints and points with a collapsed group that has an external connection.

title: Compare routes to placeholder code when the editor has loaded the file.
input: Open `examples/code-from-file/orders-report.draft` with its SQL file available. The editor routes `runs` at y=113, while the Current card uses the placeholder and routes it at y=45. The base commit also uses the placeholder.
fix: Pass the file session's resolved `codeFiles()` to each source task and compile with those files.
prevent_detail: Compare the route to a named code range in the editor and in a source candidate with the same resolved file inputs.

title: Each source candidate computes drawing geometry twice.
input: `computeRoutes` positions labels and builds paths and crossing halos. The source task discards that output, then `buildStaticScene` computes it again. One draw pass took 81–172 ms in five runs on a 160-shape diagram with 80 labeled edges.
fix: Extract a helper that returns the cached routing result before drawing, and use it for worker tasks that return only that result.
prevent_detail: Instrument the route-only task in a test and assert that drawing runs only when the consumer builds the visible scene.

title: The parity test compares a fresh route result with a cache hit.
