input: Vitest runs both `runShared` calls through the worker's computation code in the Node fallback. I counted one router call because the second task reuses the first task's cache entry. Separate worker threads confirmed the lane fix, but the checked-in test leaves worker messaging and final drawn paths untested.
fix: Run the source and scene tasks through separate worker instances or isolated module caches and compare the final drawn route points.
prevent_detail: Use independent caches and the normal task entry points when testing parity between two user-visible paths.

title: A clearance slide makes an adjacent leg hug a third box
input: Route from A's left to B's right with standoff=40. The boxes are A=(0,100,73,55), B=(193,216,89,70), and C=(299,124,98,62), in x, y, width, height order. Moving the vertical run from x=295 to x=322 extends its preceding leg to run 23 px along C's bottom edge at 10 px clearance. The base route stops 4 px before C begins.
fix: Measure box clearance on all three changed segments and reject a slide that introduces a new box hug.
prevent_detail: Test a slide whose resized leg reaches a third box and assert that the move leaves no new run within the audit's box-hug threshold.

title: A nearby arrow vetoes a slide that would clear both gaps
input: With parallelPenalty=0 and the default 20 px standoff and 16 px edge gap, a top-to-top route runs at y=87 beside a box whose top is y=100. A waypoint route runs at y=97 alongside it for 115 px. The veto leaves the arrows 10 px apart. Sliding to y=80 gives them 17 px of separation, clears the box, and adds no crossing.
fix: Limit the open-space veto to parallel runs the slide would pass through and use the candidate's lane checks to enforce spacing at the destination.
prevent_detail: Test that a fixed parallel route on the box side of a candidate run allows a slide that clears both the box and the requested lane gap.

title: Source Compare still bypasses generated lanes in the pinned range
input: In hn-deploy/v0.draft, Compare routes d6 from the left of pkg while the editor routes it from the bottom. Source Compare and scene route results differ on 127 of 251 files at the reviewed commit.
fix: Include the separate Compare fix from 8a980c14. Applying it to the reviewed head in memory made all 251 route results match.
prevent_detail: Compare route points, ports, and blocked states from the scene and Current comparison tasks across the audit corpus.

title: Early lane recovery adds six crossings in full mode
input: In population/exploreda-18a2cd0ec6/v0.draft, full routing goes from three crossings on base to nine at head. Both results clear every edge, and the six extra crossings outweigh the shorter paths under the router's scoring weights.
fix: Run full routing and repair with the original lane constraints, then retry lanes that remain blocked. An in-memory probe restored three crossings and kept the same blocked edges across all 73 sources with generated lanes.
prevent_detail: Check that lane recovery preserves the full router's score on corpus diagrams where strict routing and repair already clear every edge.

title: Waypoint precheck rejects a reachable imported bend
input: With 10 px clearance and a box starting at x=150, an imported waypoint at (140.004, 30) lands on the search grid boundary at x=140. Base routes around the box. Head marks the edge blocked and draws through the box in both modes.
fix: Round the waypoint with the search grid's coordinate helper before checking whether it is inside an obstacle.
prevent_detail: Test that the waypoint precheck and grid search agree on both sides of an obstacle boundary, including coordinates accepted from imported JSON.

title: Regenerate pairs current diagram text with stale code files.
input: Open Compare on orders-report.draft, then add lines to its SQL file and update the diagram to reference lines 18–30. After the editor reloads both files, Regenerate routes `runs` to a placeholder at y=45. The editor reaches the loaded code at y=147.
fix: Capture the source, compiled scene, resolved code files, and view together when Compare opens. Use that snapshot for both the Current card and every variant on Regenerate.
prevent_detail: Send a watched source update with new code files while Compare is open and verify that Regenerate draws every card from one coherent revision.

title: The parity tests stop before Compare dispatch and final drawing.
input: The tests run the worker computation through Node's fallback with separate caches and compare raw routes. A probe cleared the candidate's collapsed view after routing and changed its drawn output while the asserted routes stayed identical.
fix: Generate the Current card through Compare's normal entry point and compare its final drawn paths with the editor's paths using separate workers.
prevent_detail: Test route parity at the drawn output of both normal dispatch paths, with independent caches and fixtures whose view or loaded files affect routing.

title: A half-pixel label shift can hide the entire arrowhead.
input: On a rightward edge across a 50 px gap, move the label “Go” from a horizontal offset of 7.5 px to 8 px. Its background jumps from 19.5 px to 36 px and hides the entire chevron. A raster probe confirmed that a 20.5 px background still fits the text and clears the painted wings at 8 px.
fix: Calculate clearance from the painted chevron, including its round stroke caps. Its wings reach 6.75 px behind the tip. The current calculation reserves 7.75 px.
prevent_detail: Rasterize labels at offsets on both sides of the fit threshold and check that every wing stays visible whenever the painted text fits with the required margin.

title: The Route 4 regression test times out under concurrent load.
input: The test runs the issue diagram’s full compound-spring fit search. It took 12.7 seconds and exceeded Vitest’s 5-second limit while the corpus probe ran. All 33 targeted tests passed with two workers after the probe finished.
fix: Use a small pinned diagram with one tight horizontal gap for the unit test. Keep the full Route 4 diagram in the render audit.
prevent_detail: Test label clearance with fixed geometry and reserve full layout searches for render checks.

title: Tight vertical labels still clip arrowhead wings.
input: The downward edge e4, “new source,” in the draftably-file-session corpus has its label centered 16 px from the tip. The 22 px background covers roughly one quarter of the painted chevron in both revisions. A raster probe with an 18.5 px background restored both wings.
fix: Apply the same clearance rule along vertical terminal segments. Trim vertical padding when the text and its margin fit.
prevent_detail: Check painted arrowhead clearance for tight labels in all four terminal directions.

title: Recipe footers read the live file after Regenerate
input: Open routing Compare on orders-report.draft, add `routing clearance=4` on disk, and regenerate. The four cards keep their original drawings, as intended. Current still draws with clearance 10, but its footer reads clearance 4 from the live file, and the Tighter clearance card says “Same as the file.”
fix: Read the Current recipe and compute each variant's recipe difference from the captured source.
prevent_detail: Update a watched file while Compare is open and verify that regenerated drawings and recipe footers describe the same revision.

title: Parity tests bypass Compare dispatch and final drawing
input: The tests exercise the worker computation through Node's fallback and compare raw routes. Dropping the collapsed view only from the dedicated Compare dispatch changed the Current card's drawn paths while the test's equality assertion still passed.
fix: Open Compare through its normal entry point and compare the Current card's final SVG paths with the editor's paths using independent workers.
prevent_detail: Run parity checks through both production dispatch paths with separate caches and a fixture whose view or resolved files affect the drawn paths.

title: Vertical trimming lets the edge line touch accented text.
input: Label a downward edge “TẮT” between two pinned boxes with a 29 px gap. The background shrinks from 21 px to 15.5 px, and the rasterized edge line touches the accent above Ắ. The original background kept them separate.
fix: Use glyph ascent and descent to bound vertical trimming, and retain the original padding when those bounds are unknown.
prevent_detail: Rasterize tight vertical labels with accents and wrapped lines, then assert that the background separates every painted glyph from the edge line.

title: Dragging a label beside a clear arrow makes its background snap wider.
input: On a rightward edge across a 50 px gap, shift “Go” 8 px toward the arrowhead and drag it from 14.5 px to 14.6 px below the line. The background jumps from 20.5 px to 36 px wide. The full arrowhead is visible at both offsets even with the original 36 px background.
fix: Check the painted chevron against the original label background before trimming. The marker viewport includes unpainted space.
prevent_detail: Sweep perpendicular label offsets and assert that the original background keeps its dimensions wherever it clears the painted marker.

title: Rejected clearance retries rescore the whole diagram
input: A diagram with 200 independent links running 11 px from nearby frames took a median 385 ms to route, up from 79 ms on the base commit. At 400 links, routing rose from 278 ms to 2.15 s. The pass scored the whole diagram 401 times and kept zero replacements.
fix: Check the clearance gain before scoring the candidate. For candidates that pass, calculate the score change from the route and the pairs it affects.
prevent_detail: Use a large diagram with crowded routes and zero acceptable replacements to verify that rejected candidates do not trigger whole-diagram scoring.

title: The clearance retry skips a shorter, clearer route
input: With default options, connect the left port of A to the right port of B. Use box rectangles (x, y, w, h) A(381, 1, 94, 81), B(32, 134, 90, 67), and blockers (223, 24, 87, 85), (212, 149, 92, 73), (369, 105, 105, 62), and (145, -40, 80, 40). The retry stops at a 444 px route. Letting only the retry reach grid search produced a valid 385 px route with the same ports and four bends, and reduced the final standoff cost from 33.4 to zero.
fix: Let a clearance-only retry run the bounded grid search when its best dogleg still fails the clearance check.
prevent_detail: Test a crowded dogleg with a shorter valid grid route and assert that refinement increases clearance while preserving the locked ports and bend count.

title: A theme change can leave the edge line touching label text.
input: Place “nil” on a rightward edge across a 50 px gap, shift it 10 px toward the arrow, and switch from Drafting to Signal. The editor keeps the 16.5 px background as the font changes, so the line touches the text. A fresh SVG uses a 22.9 px background and keeps the text clear. The cache also returns stale label widths on the base branch.
fix: Include the resolved annotation font, size, and line height in the cache key for drawn routes.
prevent_detail: Switch themes in a live editor and compare its label geometry with a fresh SVG of the same document.

title: The label hit area jumps beside an already clear arrowhead.
input: On a rightward edge across a 50 px gap, shift “Go” 3 px toward the arrow and move it from 14 to 14.5 px below the line. Its background grows from 30.5 to 36 px. Raster checks show that the original 36 px rounded background clears the full arrowhead at both offsets.
fix: Trim only when the original rounded background intersects the painted chevron.
prevent_detail: Sweep label offsets past both arrow wings and assert that the background keeps its original size wherever the painted shapes clear each other.

title: The single-waypoint fallback reports routes through nodes as clear
input: Route from the right of a 100×60 box at (0, 0) to the top of a 100×60 box at (250, 200), with waypoint (150, 30) inside a third box at (140, 10) sized 50×40. The base reports the route blocked. The new fallback reports it clear because compression merges the first leg into a port stub and skips its obstacle check.
fix: Check every segment from stub to stub against the candidate obstacles before calling `remember`. This rejected the blocked route in a read-only probe and kept both Srcly returns clear.
prevent_detail: Assert that every unblocked one-waypoint route clears unrelated obstacles even when its first or last leg is collinear with a port stub.

title: Pinning one node in place removes the return gutter for the whole group
input: Add `pin jobs x=36 y=20` to the Srcly scan fixture. That is the node's current local position. The frame still shrinks from 546px to 510px, the other five nodes move 36px left, and the unrelated `dispatch` return becomes blocked. A `stay` at the same position has the same effect.
fix: Compute the gutter from the unrefined fold and apply it to automatic positions before resolving pins and stays in content coordinates. Use each band's turn counts and extrema to reserve room without running the lane-order search twice.
prevent_detail: Pin an unrelated member at its computed position and assert that the frame, sibling positions, and return routes remain unchanged.

title: A return into a nested group can run through its parent's title band
input: Put eight 180×100 nodes in a chain under a group with `flow direction=down`, and put the fifth node in a subgroup. The return from the fourth node turns at y=28 inside the parent title band and is blocked on both commits. Nudging the parent's immediate children down 12px clears the route.
fix: Include descendant endpoints when computing each folded group's turn extents. Reserve top room through the bottom of the parent title obstacle.
prevent_detail: Exercise folded rows and columns that enter a nested group and assert that the return clears both title bands.

title: Fixed turn spacing leaves too little room for higher clearance
input: Add `routing clearance=26` to the Srcly scan fixture. The `rollup` track runs 20px from the boxes it passes, and the edge remains blocked on both commits. An in-memory probe with a 30px lane pitch clears both returns.
fix: Use the router's clearance and stub length to set the minimum turn offset and band gap. Size the frame from the turns that the router will use.
prevent_detail: Check folded returns at the default and upper supported clearances and assert that each route stays inside its frame and clears the intervening boxes.

title: Clearance refinement keeps two bends that cleanup would remove
input: With default options, connect A’s left port to B’s right port. Use rectangles (x, y, w, h) A(409, -18, 83, 85), B(7, 143, 94, 80), and blockers (200, 30, 87, 96), (232, 154, 81, 87), (382, 86, 114, 65), and (155, -23, 95, 33). The retry lowers the routing cost from 603.5 to 594.5 before cleanup. Cleanup removes a jog from the original route, so the base returns two bends at a cost of 535. The new route keeps four bends at a cost of 594.5 and still costs more after including its clearance gain.
fix: Apply the same jog cleanup to the original and replacement before accepting a clearance-only retry.
prevent_detail: Compare the final output of RouteLab.compute with and without clearance refinement on a fixture where cleanup can remove a jog from the original route.

title: A clearer dogleg stops grid search even when the cost check rejects it
input: Use rectangles A(399, 27, 89, 79), B(17, 147, 97, 77), C(242, 0, 95, 88), D(207, 125, 100, 70), E(389, 102, 106, 56), and F(166, -17, 82, 43), with automatic links A→B, D→B, and C→D. With tidy disabled, the A→B dogleg lowers standoff cost from 27.41 to 6.91 but raises drawing cost from 827 to 847. The retry rejects it after grid search has already stopped. Letting the bounded search continue produces a valid route with standoff cost 5.16 and drawing cost 721.
fix: Use the same clearance and routing-cost checks to decide whether a dogleg can end the bounded search and whether it can replace the original route.
prevent_detail: Exercise a clearance retry where the dogleg meets the clearance target but exceeds the cost limit, and assert that the search can still return a qualifying grid route.

title: The single-waypoint fallback can draw an edge that crosses itself
input: Route from a 100×60 box at (0, 140) to a 100×60 box at (230, 70), with a 90×60 obstacle at (440, 230). Keep both ports automatic and add a waypoint at (425, 280). The fallback marks the route clear even though it crosses itself at (280, 170). Another candidate passes through the same waypoint without a loop.
fix: Reuse the existing conflict check on the two compressed halves, including the port stubs. Reject candidates whose halves cross or overlap beyond their shared waypoint. An in-memory probe selected the loop-free candidate and kept both Srcly returns clear.
prevent_detail: Add a manual-waypoint routing test that checks the route visits the waypoint, clears obstacles, and has no self-intersections.

title: A folded return into a subgroup can hit the parent title band
input: Put eight 180×100 nodes in a chain in a group with `flow direction=down` and place the fifth node in a subgroup. The return from the fourth node turns at y=28, inside the parent title band, and is blocked on both commits. Moving the parent's immediate children down 12 px clears it.
fix: Include descendant endpoints when sizing fold turns and reserve enough top room for the return to pass below the parent title obstacle.
prevent_detail: Check folded rows and columns with a return into a subgroup and assert that the route clears both title bands.

title: Fixed fold spacing blocks returns at higher clearance
input: Add `routing clearance=26` to the Srcly scan fixture. The 20 px turn offset puts the `rollup` track inside the required clearance, so the edge stays blocked on both commits. It also stays blocked at the supported maximum of 30 px.
fix: Use the router's clearance and stub length to size the turn offsets and the gap between bands. Reserve frame room from those same offsets.
prevent_detail: Test folded returns at the default and maximum supported clearances and assert that each route stays inside the frame and clears intervening boxes.

title: An unremovable jog suppresses a clearance retry.
input: With default options, connect A’s left port to B’s right port. Use rectangles (x, y, w, h) A(414, 36, 97, 55), B(12, 129, 113, 74), C(191, 9, 113, 58), D(213, 151, 86, 99), and E(379, 87, 103, 80). A 13.5 px jog skips the retry, and cleanup makes no move. Removing only the skip in the probe reduced the standoff cost from 36.11 to zero at the same 519.5 drawing cost.
fix: Compare against the incumbent after valid jog cleanup. Continue the clearance retry when cleanup cannot remove the jog.
prevent_detail: Exercise removable and unremovable jogs through the full router and check the final clearance and drawing cost.

title: The retry can discard a qualifying route after searching for it.
input: With tidy disabled, use rectangles A(187, 284, 103, 101), B(174, 11, 82, 70), C(189, 153, 82, 89), and D(23, 307, 108, 58), with automatic links A→B and D→A. The bounded search runs but returns the crowded A→B route again. Applying the clearance and cost checks during candidate selection found a route that lowered standoff cost from 29.69 to 8.90 and drawing cost from 457.5 to 453.5, with zero crossings and lane conflicts.
fix: Check the final geometry of each candidate against the retry criteria before it can become the best candidate or narrow the search.
prevent_detail: Test a retry where the generic score favors the incumbent but another candidate meets both the clearance and drawing cost checks.

title: The wider jog cleanup moves an explicit target port offset.
input: Use rectangles A(382, 18, 80, 93), B(-6, 151, 113, 84), C(238, 50, 90, 103), and D(201, 117, 80, 68). Connect A’s left port to B’s right port with toOffset set to 0 and passes set to 1. The base lands at y=193. The new cleanup removes a 12 px jog and lands at y=205. Setting jogs to false preserves y=193.
fix: Protect the explicit target offset when validating tidy moves, including jog cleanup.
prevent_detail: Run the same explicit-offset fixture with quick routing and full cleanup and assert that both keep the requested target point.

title: Theme switches can leave live routes out of sync with fresh exports.
input: Open the RAG benchmark as a standalone document and switch from Drafting to Fieldnotes. Chromium showed three raw routes differ from a fresh render, and the i3 label sits 24 px lower. The same mismatch occurs when switching from Signal to Ink. The typography change triggers routing with the previous theme’s port choices.
fix: When typography changes, compute raw routes with the same inputs as a fresh export, including an empty list of prior routes.
prevent_detail: Switch themes on a grouped diagram and compare live raw routes and SVG label bounds with a fresh export after each switch.

title: Recoloring a node moves unrelated routes and labels.
input: In the standalone RAG benchmark, recolor the user node red. The full fingerprint invalidates the drawing cache and reruns the router. Chromium showed three routes change and the i3 label move down 24 px. The parent commit keeps the routes and label in place.
fix: Key the drawing cache on geometry inputs and exclude paint-only style fields such as color and shade.
prevent_detail: Apply paint-only edits through the session and assert that the cached routes and drawn label bounds stay identical.

title: The drawing cache ignores a replacement route result for the same fingerprint.
input: A direct probe supplied two adopted results for the same document fingerprint, with different port sides in the second result. The cache kept drawing the first result because both the fingerprint and ready flag stayed equal. The parent behaved the same way.
fix: Include the adopted result’s identity in the cache check when ready is true.
prevent_detail: Adopt two distinct route results for the same document and assert that the canvas draws the latest result.

title: Fold padding makes an unpinned node overlap a pinned node.
input: Add `pin scan x=168 y=48` to Srcly scan. The pin holds, but the new 36 px gutter moves `jobs` into `scan`. The boxes overlap by 32 × 8 px on the reviewed commit. The base leaves them 4 px apart.
fix: If leading fold padding introduces an overlap during refinement, retry the scope without that padding. Keep the pin fixed and compute the lanes from the resulting boxes.
prevent_detail: Pin a node beside the proposed fold gutter and assert that the pin holds and its unpinned neighbors remain disjoint.

title: A folded return into a subgroup remains blocked by the parent title band.
input: Put eight 180 × 100 nodes in a `flow direction=down` chain and place the fifth node in a subgroup. The fourth-to-fifth return plans a horizontal turn at y=28 inside the parent title band on both commits. Moving the parent’s immediate children down 12 px clears the route.
fix: Include subgroup descendants when sizing fold turns and reserve enough top space to put the horizontal run below the parent title obstacle.
prevent_detail: Check folded rows and columns with a return into a subgroup and assert that each return clears both title bands.

title: Fixed fold spacing still blocks returns at supported clearances.
input: Add `routing clearance=26` or `routing clearance=30` to Srcly scan. Both returns are blocked on both commits. The planner still uses 20 px turn offsets.
fix: Derive the turn offsets and minimum band gap from the router’s clearance and stub length. Use those same dimensions to size the frame.
prevent_detail: Route a folded fan-out at default and maximum supported clearance and assert that every return stays inside the frame and clears the obstacles.

title: A pinned subgroup can put the return turn outside its frame
input: Add `routing clearance=30` and `pin sub x=0 y=184` to the right-reading subgroup fixture. The pin restores the subgroup to the left inset after layout reserves room. The final turn lands at x=-9, outside the parent frame, and e3 is blocked. The base revision routes e3 inside the frame.
fix: Check generated turns against the owning frame after refinements. Let the router choose a free path when a turn falls outside, and keep the authored pin.
prevent_detail: Test pinned folded subgroups at supported clearances and assert that valid routes stay inside the final frame.

title: Downward folds place subgroup turns inside the parent title band
input: Add `routing clearance=19` or `routing clearance=30` to the downward subgroup fixture. The return turn stays at y=48, while the parent title obstacle extends to y=49 or y=60. At 30 px, shifting the folded contents down 12 px made e3 route cleanly.
fix: Size the top gutter from the router's clearance-expanded title boundary so the first return turn can clear it.
prevent_detail: Sweep supported clearances in both fold directions with plain and wrapped parent titles, and assert that each return clears the router's obstacles.

title: Cell routing can force a port opposite the fold turn
input: In the right-reading subgroup fixture, put n4 in a nested `cells` group and set `routing clearance=30`. The fold approaches from the left, while cell routing forces n4's right port. Both revisions block e3. Using the cell's free left port clears it.
fix: Use the fold's approach to choose the cell port when that side is free. Otherwise, choose a path for the available cell port.
prevent_detail: Route folds into outline and interior cells, and assert that each route reaches a valid port from its planned approach.

title: Renaming a group can leave a connection crossing its new title.
input: In a standalone diagram, connect a node above a group to a node inside it. Rename the group from “G” to “Monitoring queues and distributed services” without resizing it. The live edge keeps crossing the title at x=100, while a fresh export routes around it and moves the label.
fix: Include measured group title obstacles in the live cache key, using the same geometry the router and label placer read.
prevent_detail: Rename a group without changing its frame and compare live raw routes and label bounds with a fresh export.

title: Recoloring a node still moves routes after a comparison result is adopted.
input: Apply the tighter-clearance routing candidate to the standalone RAG benchmark, then recolor the Support agent node red. The adopted fingerprint stops matching. Three unrelated routes change and the “upsert” label moves down 24 px on both commits.
fix: Exclude paint-only style fields from the adoption fingerprint while retaining style fields that affect routing geometry.
prevent_detail: Apply a routing candidate, change only a node's color or shade, and assert that the adopted routes and label bounds stay identical.

title: A paint-only file edit redraws every connection when equivalent routes arrive.
input: Change only the theme text color in the 28-node, 29-edge xl-triggers benchmark. All 10 edits kept the same routing fingerprint and geometry, but each new worker result object forced a full redraw. In the simulated worker delivery probe this took 22–42 ms per edit, compared with 1–4 ms on the base commit.
fix: Reuse drawn routes when a replacement result has equivalent route geometry. Redraw when the route payload changes and update report data separately.
prevent_detail: Deliver equivalent and changed worker route payloads for one fingerprint and assert that only the changed payload invalidates drawn geometry.

title: Pinning a subgroup can put a downward return inside the title band
input: In the eight-step downward subgroup fixture, set `routing clearance=30` and `pin sub x=264 y=44`. The final turn is at y=59, one pixel inside the parent title band. The frame check accepts it and e3 is blocked. The base routes e3, and removing the generated lane lets the reviewed revision route inside the frame with the pin intact. The pin and stay sweep found 47 newly blocked cases out of 744.
fix: Validate downward turns against the final clearance-expanded title band using the router's title geometry. Discard an invalid generated lane so the router can choose another path while keeping the authored pin.
prevent_detail: Sweep pin and stay positions around the title-band boundary at supported clearances and assert that returns stay inside the frame, route successfully, and preserve valid anchors.

title: Cell routing can force a port opposite the fold turn
input: In the right-reading subgroup fixture, put n4 in a nested `cells` group and set `routing clearance=30`. The fold approaches from the left, while cell routing forces n4's right port and blocks e3 on both revisions. Selecting the free left port clears the route inside the frame.
fix: Use the fold's approach when it reaches a free side of the cell. When that side is unavailable, route through an available side or the cell's outline stub.
prevent_detail: Route folds into outline and interior cells and assert that each path reaches a valid port or stub from its planned approach.

title: Switching to Fieldnotes moves routes on a diagram with no groups.
input: Open the org chart as a standalone document, drag the CEO box 120 px right and down, then switch from Drafting to Fieldnotes. The routing input stays identical, but four connections move and r4 leaves from the bottom instead of the right. The base revision preserves all four routes.
fix: Include group title metrics only where they affect connection geometry, and preserve prior routes when that geometry stays the same.
prevent_detail: After a drag, switch between themes with identical connection geometry and assert that the live routes and label bounds stay unchanged.

title: Removing a code caption leaves a connection attached to the old line position.
input: Remove the caption from a standalone two-line code node with a connection to its second line. The node rectangle stays fixed, and the live endpoint stays at y=62 while a fresh export puts it at y=36. The live edge label also stays at its old position.
fix: Key the live route cache on the measured range ports and obstacles, which include the caption band's effect.
prevent_detail: Add and remove a code caption at a fixed node size and compare the live range endpoint and edge label bounds with a fresh export.

title: Fold clearance can block a return into a pinned subgroup’s cell.
input: In the eight-step downward fixture, place n4 in a nested cells row with a second cell sized 100 by 70 px. Set routing clearance=30 and pin sub x=264 y=48. The base routes e3 into n4’s left port. The new gutter moves n3 down 45 px, so the router selects n4’s bottom port, which n5 blocks. Disabling the gutter shift or selecting the left port restores the route with the pin intact.
fix: Treat automatic cell sides as preferences for folded returns. If the preferred port is blocked, try the other free outline ports before marking the return blocked.
prevent_detail: Sweep pins and supported clearances on folds into multi-cell groups, and assert that returns use reachable ports while preserving the pins.

title: Cell routing can force a port opposite the fold turn.
input: In the unpinned right-reading fixture, place n4 in a nested cells group and set routing clearance=30. The fold approaches from the left, but cell routing forces the right port and blocks e3 on both commits. Selecting the free left port clears the route inside the frame.
fix: Use the fold’s approach to choose among free outline ports. For interior cells, use the same approach to choose the outline stub.
prevent_detail: Route folds into outline and interior cells and assert that each return reaches a valid port or stub from its planned approach.

title: The Worker no longer enforces the pixel cap after adding the source strip.
input: At scale 3, examples/order-pipeline.draft starts at 7,944,318 pixels and grows to 8,020,413 after the strip. The parent commit rejects it, but this commit renders it. Six of 311 tracked files cross the cap at a supported scale. GET, REST, MCP, and share image requests use this path. The spans still record raw and embedded PNG byte counts, but the request log now keeps the smaller pre-strip pixel count.
fix: Keep the pre-strip check and validate the final SVG before resvg allocates the image. Use the final pixel count in the request log.
prevent_detail: Test a diagram that fits before the strip but exceeds the cap after it, and assert that the Worker rejects it before rasterization.

title: Client metadata can change after sign-in validation and cause a callback redirect before consent.
input: A Client ID Metadata Document permits the request at verification, then changes its authorization policy while retaining the registered callback. The following GET parses against the new metadata and can send an OAuth error to the callback before showing consent. This sends no authorization code or session cookie.
fix: Give the post-sign-in continuation a local-only error path. If the authorization no longer parses, send the browser to `/account` and do not use the provider's callback redirect.
prevent_detail: Test that the sign-in continuation stays on-site when client metadata changes between verification and consent.

title: A raw line break in `next` spends the sign-in token without returning a session cookie.
input: A workerd probe passed an otherwise valid continuation with a literal line break in its query. The request URL parser removed the line break, but the raw `Location` header threw after the token and session writes. Retrying the same token returned 400.
fix: Build `Location` from the same parsed URL used for validation, or reject noncanonical input and continue to `/account`.
prevent_detail: Test that noncanonical continuation URLs produce either a usable same-origin redirect or `/account`, with the session cookie in both cases.

title: Rejected continuations do not land on the account page.
input: A sign-in continuation with an unsupported response type, invalid resource, or missing PKCE challenge returns a local 400 at `/authorize`. No callback fires, but the browser never reaches `/account` as specified.
fix: When the resumed GET rejects an authorization request, redirect to `/account`. Keep transient metadata failures on a local retry page.
prevent_detail: Follow the actual sign-in redirect and assert the final path for accepted requests, rejected requests, and temporary provider failures.

title: The success proof skips the redirect returned by sign-in.
input: The proof checks the marked `Location` but fetches the original unmarked URL for consent. An in-memory negative control that returned 400 for every marked GET passed these checks while breaking the real continuation.
fix: Fetch the sign-in response's `Location` with the new session cookie for the first successful consent check.
prevent_detail: In redirect flow tests, use the URL and cookies returned by the preceding response rather than rebuilding the next request from fixture input.

title: GET /link creates a public share even when the supplied key is wrong
input: A fresh diagram sent to GET /link with an invalid bearer key returned 200 and created a share row. POST /v1/share refused the same key with 401 ERR_AUTH.
fix: Check any supplied key before calling urlSource or createShare, as POST /v1/share does.
prevent_detail: Send a wrong key with a fresh source through every share entry point and assert 401 with no row written.

title: MCP link tools silently drop the requested PNG scale
input: Both image_url and share_diagram dropped scale: 1 and returned PNG links at the default scale of 2. The image_url link drew a 3,752-byte PNG while REST drew a 1,684-byte PNG for the same source at scale 1.
fix: Add scale to both link tool schemas and pass it to readRequest so the generated URLs retain it.
prevent_detail: Fetch the URLs returned by each link tool at a non-default scale and compare their PNG bytes with a direct render.

title: MCP returns REST errors for malformed protocol requests
input: An authenticated text/plain POST changed from 415 to 400 ERR_SOURCE. A truncated JSON body lost JSON-RPC parse code -32700 and received a REST error object instead. Valid batches and notifications kept their prior behavior.
fix: Use the SDK's bounded reader with MAX_BODY so it still checks headers and formats parse errors. Map only its size refusal to ERR_TOO_LARGE.
prevent_detail: Assert MCP status and JSON-RPC error shape for malformed JSON, unsupported media types, and oversized bodies.

title: A BOM changes the 64 KiB cutoff by transport
input: A valid 65,536-byte source with a leading UTF-8 BOM returned 200 through REST but 400 ERR_SOURCE through its compressed GET URL. GET counts decompressed bytes before stripping the BOM, while REST strips it first.
fix: Apply the same raw byte limit before BOM removal on all transports and keep the decompression bound.
prevent_detail: Compare encoded GET, REST, MCP, and share behavior just below, at, and above the source limit, with and without a BOM.

title: Account and consent forms bypass the shared POST body limit
input: A same-origin 300 KiB POST to /login reached email validation and returned 400 instead of 413. Account and consent handlers still call formData() directly, outside the 256 KiB reader.
fix: Apply the shared byte limit before parsing forms, while keeping existing origin and session checks ahead of body reads.
prevent_detail: Send an oversized body to every POST handler that reads one, including forms, and assert 413 before parsing.

title: Valid YAML comments change the title and drop the dark theme
input: Mermaid reads `title: "Checkout flow" # navigation label` as Checkout flow and `theme: "dark" # night view` under `config` as dark. The importer keeps literal quotes in the title and warns that the theme was ignored. A folded title becomes the literal `>-`, and ignored keys with list, null, or empty-map values can disappear from the warning.
fix: Use a YAML reader with Mermaid's schema. Read `title` and nested `config.theme` from the parsed values, and collect ignored keys from the same parsed mapping.
prevent_detail: Compare imported metadata with Mermaid on shared fixtures that cover comments, multiline values, and non-scalar settings.

title: A valid escape in an ignored setting rejects the render
input: Mermaid accepts `notes: "Caf\xE9"` above a flowchart. The frontmatter reader calls `JSON.parse` before the error handler. Both the service adapter and the drop-in reject with a raw `SyntaxError` instead of drawing the chart and warning about `notes`.
fix: Read frontmatter inside the guarded parse phase with a YAML reader that supports YAML escapes. Convert actual parse failures to import diagnostics.
prevent_detail: Assert that valid ignored metadata never rejects a render and that malformed metadata returns a diagnostic instead of throwing.

title: Frontmatter boundary rules disagree across entry points
input: With CR-only line endings, explicit import succeeds but the service's automatic path treats the same source as Draftably. An indented `---` inside a YAML block scalar also ends the local scan early, so detection and import miss a flowchart that Mermaid accepts.
fix: Share one frontmatter scanner across detection, import, and the Markdown candidate check. Normalize line endings and match the closing fence at the opening fence's indentation.
prevent_detail: Have each entry point use the same normalized diagram-body boundary before it decides whether to import the source.

title: The dark theme can split a quoted title
input: A title of `"First\u2028Second"` imports without a theme. With `config.theme: dark`, the splice treats the Unicode separator as a line break and inserts `theme blueprint` inside the quoted title. Native validation then reports an unclosed string.
fix: Emit the theme through the native source serializer after the diagram declaration.
prevent_detail: Assert that adding a theme preserves the decoded title and produces valid native source for titles with quotes and Unicode separators.

title: Timeline imports drop the frontmatter title
input: A timeline with `title: Project history` in frontmatter and no body title uses the fallback title in the importer and renders without a title in the service and drop-in. Mermaid's timeline database exposes its title setter through `getCommonDb()`, so passing metadata to `getDiagramFromText` does not set it.
fix: Use the frontmatter title as the timeline fallback when the body did not set a title.
prevent_detail: For each supported diagram family, assert that a frontmatter title reaches native source and that a body title overrides it.

title: Ignored YAML can still cause an import error
input: A valid YAML value such as `notes: 'Docs'` parses locally, but Mermaid rewrites the HTML attribute quotes before reading the YAML again and rejects the chart. A note that merely quotes `%%{init}%%` also triggers the directive refusal, even though the diagram body contains no directive.
fix: Parse the metadata once and give Mermaid only the diagram body and the supported title. Check for directives in the diagram body and preserve source line offsets for diagnostics.
prevent_detail: Assert that valid ignored metadata containing diagram-like text yields one warning and leaves the drawing unchanged.

title: A code fence in YAML can replace the real diagram
input: Put an indented Mermaid code fence inside a `notes: |` block and a different flowchart after the frontmatter. The service renders only the example in the note, even with `type=mermaid`. CLI detection does the same for a `.txt` file, while `.mmd` detection imports the real chart.
fix: Recognize a raw Mermaid source with valid frontmatter before scanning for Markdown fences. Keep the original source when its diagram body has a Mermaid signature.
prevent_detail: Compare the selected source across automatic, explicit, and extension-based import for a fixture with a Markdown example inside YAML.

title: Ignored YAML aliases can make the warning walk fail
input: The YAML reader can return an ignored mapping that refers to itself through an alias. `settingPaths` assumes mappings form a tree and recurses without a guard, so warning collection can throw before the importer returns native source.
fix: Stop descent at a repeated ancestor and cap the number of paths collected. Name the skipped setting in the same warning.
prevent_detail: Require metadata walkers at input boundaries to track visited ancestors and enforce a work limit.

title: Automatic detection misses bare Mermaid graphs that start with a decision node
input: Add frontmatter above `graph\n  A{Proceed?} --> B`. The DOT check reads `graph A{` across the newline, so automatic service rendering fails while explicit Mermaid rendering works. If the YAML also contains a Mermaid fence, the service renders that example instead of the real graph.
fix: Use a Mermaid-specific header check on the body after frontmatter, without sending it back through the generic DOT check.
prevent_detail: Compare the selected body and render result across automatic, explicit, and extension-based import for frontmatter charts with ambiguous headers.

title: An empty body title can bring back the frontmatter title
input: Set `title: Outer` in frontmatter and write `title <T>` in a sequence diagram. Mermaid sanitizes the body title to an empty string and keeps it empty. The importer restores `Outer`.
fix: Keep Mermaid's final title for families that accept title metadata. For timelines, distinguish a missing body title from one that resolves to an empty string.
prevent_detail: Test title precedence with both visible body titles and body titles that sanitize to empty.

title: An escaped title can import successfully but fail to render
input: A YAML title of `"First\fSecond"` imports without a warning. The decoded form feed is not valid in SVG text, so the runtime rejects the converted diagram with `DRAFT_TEXT_INVALID`.
fix: Use the runtime's XML text rule on the decoded title before emitting native source, and report any text removed or replaced.
prevent_detail: Send imported titles with YAML escapes through the SVG renderer and assert that accepted imports produce valid SVG.

title: A literal dotted key can disappear from the ignored-settings warning
input: Include both `config: {theme: dark}` and the top-level key `"config.theme": unrelated`. The nested value maps to Blueprint, but the import gives no warning for the ignored top-level key.
fix: Keep key segments separate until after filtering the supported settings, then format the remaining paths for the warning.
prevent_detail: Test that a literal key containing a dot and a nested path with the same spelling remain distinct.

title: Labeling a primary line can give its subtree to a secondary line
input: Use `r -> a`, `a -> b`, `r -> b "also"`, and `b -> c`. Add a label to `a -> b` in the editor. The saved source changes only the label, but BFS now picks `r -> b`. Bob moves up a row in the org chart, and Bob and Child switch sides in the mind map.
fix: Select tree parents without using label text. Mark secondary lines explicitly with `constraint=false` or `kind=async`, and have Connect write a secondary line that cannot replace the current parent.
prevent_detail: Toggle labels on every edge in a two-parent fixture and assert that tree parents, rows, and sides stay fixed.

title: A short label can float above its mind-map branch
input: Compile a two-node mind map with `edge e r -> a "interim"`. The branch stays in the tree, but its label sits 44.5 px above the only line. The same label missed its line on 3 of the 11 branches in the shipped mind-map example.
fix: Reserve enough clear space for branch labels in the mind-map layout, or route the branch through a clear label position without changing its parent or side.
prevent_detail: Assert that a typical label's box intersects its own rendered route on a two-node map with no other lines.

title: Quick extend turns a split tree branch into a cross-link
input: Select the line from the root to its only child and use quick extend to insert a step. The split clears the first segment's projected head, so the writer adds `head=arrow` and neither segment stays in the tree. This also happens with an unlabeled branch on the base commit.
fix: Keep the first segment's inferred headless state when splitting a tree line. Write `head=arrow` only when the user chooses an arrow.
prevent_detail: Add the edge-target quick-extend action to the file round-trip matrix and assert that both saved segments stay in the tree.

title: A plain back edge can cut off a labeled subtree
input: Use `r -> a "interim"`, `a -> b`, and `b -> a`. The plain back edge blocks `r -> a` before BFS starts, even though BFS cannot reach `b` without it. Both nodes fall out of the tree. A plain line from an otherwise disconnected node has the same effect.
fix: Keep labeled candidates available and give a plain parent priority only if it can reach the target from the root without using that target.
prevent_detail: Test a labeled entry into a cycle and a competing plain edge from an unreachable node, and assert that both subtrees stay reachable.

title: A labeled line parallel to a plain branch draws as another branch
input: Write `edge main r -> a` and `edge extra r -> a "also"`. The candidate filter keeps `extra` out of the tree, but the same-end rule marks it as a branch anyway. It loses its arrowhead in both layouts and joins the reporting bus in the org chart.
fix: Limit the same-end exception to matched old and new lines in a comparison. Draw ordinary parallel edges according to their selected tree role.
prevent_detail: Test that a parallel labeled edge does not get branch styling or a bus route unless it is a matched comparison edge.

title: Compare strips the arrowhead from a renamed org-chart cross-link
input: Keep `r -> a -> b` as the reporting tree and change only the text on `r -> b "also"`. Both standalone files draw the cross-link with an arrowhead. Compare marks it changed and draws it headless even though it was never a reporting line.
fix: Use the edge's actual reporting role in each source version to set its head. A change mark alone does not establish that role.
prevent_detail: Compare each panel's branch flags and effective arrowheads with its standalone source, including a label-only cross-link edit.

title: A labeled shortcut replaces an existing tree line
input: Write `r -> a`, `a -> b`, `b -> c`, then `r -> b "advises"`. The base keeps the last line as a cross-link. This commit makes it the parent line and moves B and its subtree in both layouts.
fix: Keep labels out of parent selection. Use an explicit secondary role and migrate existing cross-links to it, or revise the stated invariant if that syntax change is intentional.
prevent_detail: Test an existing labeled shortcut into a subtree and toggle labels on both incoming lines while checking parent, row, and side.

title: An assistant's reporting label can miss its line
input: Give a CEO one `role=assistant` report and label the reporting line `"reports directly"`. The line stays in the tree, but the label wraps and floats beside the stem. The same label misses line `r1` in the shipped org chart.
fix: Reserve room for the label on the assistant's own leg without changing the report's row or side.
prevent_detail: Check that labels on row, assistant, and stacked reporting lines intersect their own rendered routes.

title: Quick extend takes a split branch out of the tree
input: Select a tree line and use Quick extend. The save adds `head=arrow` to the first segment, so neither segment remains in the tree. The probe reproduced this with a labeled line and with an unlabeled line on the base.
fix: Preserve the branch's inferred headless state on both segments. Write `head=arrow` only when the user chooses an arrow.
prevent_detail: Add edge-target Quick extend to the file edit matrix and check that both saved segments stay in the tree.

title: Connect can replace a topic's existing parent
input: Start with `r -> a -> b` and use Connect from R to B. The editor saves a plain `r -> b`, which takes over as B's parent. The compiler chose the same new parent on the base.
fix: When Connect targets a node that is already in the same tree, save the new edge as an explicit secondary line.
prevent_detail: Round-trip Connect to an existing descendant and assert that the new edge draws without changing any tree parent.

title: Compare draws a renamed cross-link as a tree line
input: Rename only the label on a second edge parallel to a branch. Both standalone files show an arrow, but both Compare panels draw it headless as a branch in either layout. An org-chart cross-link with different ends also loses its arrow at line 92.
fix: Use each source version's actual branch role in Compare. Do not infer that role from a change mark or shared endpoints.
prevent_detail: Compare each panel's branch flags and arrowheads with its standalone source after a label-only change.

title: A branch label can rotate a fitted mind map
input: Use `fit=wide` with edges `r -> a`, `r -> b`, `a -> c`, and `r -> u` in that order. Add a six-line label to `r -> a`. The same four branches remain, but the map changes from top-to-bottom to left-to-right.
fix: Choose the reading direction without label spacing, then reserve label room in the chosen layout.
prevent_detail: Toggle a multiline branch label with automatic fit enabled and check that the reading direction and relative sides do not change.

title: Pasting a cross-link drops its explicit tree exclusion
input: With `r -> a -> b`, copy and paste `r -> b "advises" constraint=false`. Paste drops `constraint=false`. The base already lost the attribute, but the pasted labeled line now takes over as B's parent. A pasted `kind=async` line stays secondary.
fix: Carry the authored tree exclusion through projection and the clipboard, then write it back when saving the pasted edge.
prevent_detail: Round-trip a solid cross-link through copy and paste and check that the copy retains its source constraint and stays outside the tree.

title: A label stacks unrelated reports in a default org chart.
input: Give a CEO one manager and that manager four leaf reports. Use the default org chart with no fit setting. Adding "Reports directly" to the CEO-to-manager line changes the four leaves from one row to two, although none of their lines has a label. The preceding commit kept one row.
fix: Choose the leaf modes before reserving label space. Widen only the assistant or stacked leg that carries the label.
prevent_detail: Toggle a label on a manager's incoming line and assert that the default chart keeps the same report rows and sides.

title: Compare still removes arrowheads from cross-links.
input: In an org chart with R → A → B, rename the label on a separate B → R link. Both standalone files draw its arrowhead, but neither Compare panel does. Adding a labeled second R → A line also turns that cross-link into a headless branch in Compare in both layouts.
fix: Use each standalone version's branch flags and heads in its panel. Do not infer an edge's role from its change mark or endpoints.
prevent_detail: Compare edge roles and arrowheads in each panel against its standalone scene after an edge rename, addition, or removal.

title: Multiline reporting labels can still miss their lines.
input: With leaves=stack, give a manager four reports and put five lines of text on each reporting line. The second and fourth labels sit left of the stem and do not touch their routes. A single vertical reporting line with the three-line label "Interim\nChief of Staff\nUntil May" also misses its route.
fix: Reserve vertical space as well as width. Use label height to set clearance on vertical legs and between adjacent labeled stacked legs.
prevent_detail: Check that multiline labels on vertical and adjacent stacked reporting lines intersect their own rendered routes.

title: Quick extend removes a split branch from the tree.
input: Select a branch and use Quick extend. The editor saves head=arrow on the first segment, so neither segment stays in the tree. This also happens with an unlabeled branch on the base.
fix: Keep both segments plain when splitting a tree line. Write an explicit arrow only when the user chooses one.
prevent_detail: Split a tree edge in file mode and assert that both saved segments remain in the tree.

title: Connect can replace an existing tree parent.
input: Start with R → A → B and use Connect from R to B. The new plain line replaces A → B as B's parent on both the base and this commit.
fix: When Connect targets a node already in the same tree, save the new line as an explicit cross-link.
prevent_detail: Connect to an existing descendant in file mode and assert that the saved file preserves its parent.

title: Paste drops an explicit tree exclusion.
input: With R → A → B, copy and paste R → B labeled "Peer review" with constraint=false. Both the base and this commit drop constraint=false from the copy. Under the new label rule, the copy then takes over as B's parent.
fix: Carry the authored constraint through projection and the clipboard, then write it back on paste.
prevent_detail: Copy and paste an explicit cross-link and assert that the copy preserves its constraint and stays outside the tree.

title: A port swap can add a crossing to a previously clear edge pair
input: In the tracked Srcly scan lifecycle diagram, full routing swaps the bottom ports of `find` and `rollup`. The total crossing count falls, so the swap passes even though `find` gains a new intersection with the unchanged `dispatch` fallback at (1009, 124). The new intersection remains in the final route.
fix: Compare crossing counts for each affected pair after compressing the proposed routes. Require the swapped pair to improve and reject any increase involving a third edge.
prevent_detail: Add a full-routing regression that checks each affected edge pair for new crossings when a swap lowers the diagram-wide count.

title: Sliding a straight edge moves its far port off a diamond vertex
input: With `routing standoff=0`, pin a 120×96 hub at (0, 92), a 120×120 diamond at (205, 80), and a 100×60 return box at (350, 0). Route the hub's right side to the diamond's left side and the return box's bottom to the hub's right side.
